tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Step 1: Validate Prerequisites and Extract Requirements

## STEP GOAL:

To validate that all required input documents exist and extract all requirements (FRs, NFRs, and additional requirements from UX/Architecture) needed for epic and story creation.

## MANDATORY EXECUTION RULES (READ FIRST):

### Universal Rules:

- 🛑 NEVER generate content without user input
- 📖 CRITICAL: Read the complete step file before taking any action
- 🔄 CRITICAL: When loading next step with 'C', ensure entire file is read

### Role Reinforcement:

### Step-Specific Rules:

- 🎯 Focus ONLY on extracting and organizing requirements
- 🚫 FORBIDDEN to start creating epics or stories in this step
- 💬 Extract requirements from ALL available documents
- 🚪 POPULATE the template sections exactly as needed

## EXECUTION PROTOCOLS:

- 🎯 Extract requirements systematically from all documents
- 💾 Populate {planning_artifacts}/epics.md with extracted requirements
- 📖 Update frontmatter with extraction progress
- 🚫 FORBIDDEN to load next step until user selects 'C' and requirements are extracted

## REQUIREMENTS EXTRACTION PROCESS:

### 1. Welcome and Overview

Welcome {user_name} to comprehensive epic and story creation!

**CRITICAL PREREQUISITE VALIDATION:**

Verify required documents exist and are complete:

1. **PRD.md** - Contains requirements (FRs and NFRs) and product scope
2. **Architecture.md** - Contains technical decisions, API contracts, data models
3. **UX design contract** (if UI exists) - Contains visual identity, interaction patterns, mockups, and user flows

### 2. Document Discovery and Validation

Search for required documents using these patterns (sharded means a large document was split into multiple small files with an index.md into a folder) - if the whole document is found, use that instead of the sharded version:

**PRD Document Search Priority:**

1. `{planning_artifacts}/*prd*.md` (whole document)
2. `{planning_artifacts}/*prd*/index.md` (sharded version)

**Architecture Document Search Priority:**

1. `{planning_artifacts}/*architecture*.md` (whole document)
2. `{planning_artifacts}/*architecture*/index.md` (sharded version)

**UX Design Document Search (Optional):**

1. `{planning_artifacts}/ux-designs/ux-*/DESIGN.md` and `{planning_artifacts}/ux-designs/ux-*/EXPERIENCE.md` (bmad-ux spine pair)
2. `{planning_artifacts}/*ux*.md` (legacy whole document)
3. `{planning_artifacts}/*ux*/index.md` (legacy sharded version)

For each matching bmad-ux run folder, treat `DESIGN.md` and `EXPERIENCE.md` as one UX design contract:

- Confirm and load both files together. `DESIGN.md` owns visual identity and design tokens; `EXPERIENCE.md` owns information architecture, behavior, states, interactions, accessibility, and journeys.
- Add both files to the `inputDocuments: []` frontmatter array.
- If only one spine exists, report the incomplete pair and ask whether the user wants to include the partial UX handoff.
- If multiple run folders match, show each run folder with the spine frontmatter `status` and `updated` values when available, then ask the user which UX design contract to include.

Before proceeding, Ask the user if there are any other documents to include for analysis, and if anything found should be excluded. Wait for user confirmation. Once confirmed, create the {planning_artifacts}/epics.md from the ../templates/epics-template.md and in the front matter list the files in the array of `inputDocuments: []`.

### 3. Extract Functional Requirements (FRs)

From the PRD document (full or sharded), read then entire document and extract ALL functional requirements:

**Extraction Method:**

- Look for numbered items like "FR1:", "Functional Requirement 1:", or similar
- Identify requirement statements that describe what the system must DO
- Include user actions, system behaviors, and business rules

**Format the FR list as:**

```
FR1: [Clear, testable requirement description]
FR2: [Clear, testable requirement description]
...
```

### 4. Extract Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs)

From the PRD document, extract ALL non-functional requirements:

**Extraction Method:**

- Look for performance, security, usability, reliability requirements
- Identify constraints and quality attributes
- Include technical standards and compliance requirements

**Format the NFR list as:**

```
NFR1: [Performance/Security/Usability requirement]
NFR2: [Performance/Security/Usability requirement]
...
```

### 5. Extract Additional Requirements from Architecture

Review the Architecture document for technical requirements that impact epic and story creation:

**Look for:**

- **Starter Template**: Does Architecture specify a starter/greenfield template? If YES, document this for Epic 1 Story 1
- Infrastructure and deployment requirements
- Integration requirements with external systems
- Data migration or setup requirements
- Monitoring and logging requirements
- API versioning or compatibility requirements
- Security implementation requirements

**IMPORTANT**: If a starter template is mentioned in Architecture, note it prominently. This will impact Epic 1 Story 1.

**Format Additional Requirements as:**

```
- [Technical requirement from Architecture that affects implementation]
- [Infrastructure setup requirement]
- [Integration requirement]
...
```

### 6. Extract UX Design Requirements (if UX document exists)

**IMPORTANT**: The UX Design Specification is a first-class input document, not supplementary material. Requirements from the UX spec must be extracted with the same rigor as PRD functional requirements.

Read the FULL UX design contract and extract ALL actionable work items. For a bmad-ux spine pair, read both `DESIGN.md` and `EXPERIENCE.md`:

**Look for:**

- **Design token work**: Color systems, spacing scales, typography tokens that need implementation or consolidation
- **Component proposals**: Reusable UI components identified in the UX spec (e.g., ConfirmActions, StatusMessage, EmptyState, FocusIndicator)
- **Visual standardization**: Semantic CSS classes, consistent color palette usage, design pattern consolidation
- **Accessibility requirements**: Contrast audit fixes, ARIA patterns, keyboard navigation, screen reader support
- **Responsive design requirements**: Breakpoints, layout adaptations, mobile-specific interactions
- **Interaction patterns**: Animations, transitions, loading states, error handling UX
- **Browser/device compatibility**: Target platforms, progressive enhancement requirements

**Format UX Design Requirements as a SEPARATE section (not merged into Additional Requirements):**

```
UX-DR1: [Actionable UX design requirement with clear implementation scope]
UX-DR2: [Actionable UX design requirement with clear implementation scope]
...
```

**🚨 CRITICAL**: Do NOT reduce UX requirements to vague summaries. Each UX-DR must be specific enough to generate a story with testable acceptance criteria. If the UX spec identifies 6 reusable components, list all 6 — not "create reusable components."

### 7. Load and Initialize Template

Load ../templates/epics-template.md and initialize {planning_artifacts}/epics.md:

1. Copy the entire template to {planning_artifacts}/epics.md
2. Replace {{project_name}} with the actual project name
3. Replace placeholder sections with extracted requirements:
   - {{fr_list}} → extracted FRs
   - {{nfr_list}} → extracted NFRs
   - {{additional_requirements}} → extracted additional requirements (from Architecture)
   - {{ux_design_requirements}} → extracted UX Design Requirements (if UX document exists)
4. Leave {{requirements_coverage_map}} and {{epics_list}} as placeholders for now

### 8. Present Extracted Requirements

Display to user:

**Functional Requirements Extracted:**

- Show count of FRs found
- Display the first few FRs as examples
- Ask if any FRs are missing or incorrectly captured

**Non-Functional Requirements Extracted:**

- Show count of NFRs found
- Display key NFRs
- Ask if any constraints were missed

**Additional Requirements (Architecture):**

- Summarize technical requirements from Architecture
- Verify completeness

**UX Design Requirements (if applicable):**

- Show count of UX-DRs found
- Display key UX Design requirements (design tokens, components, accessibility)
- Verify each UX-DR is specific enough for story creation

### 9. Get User Confirmation

Ask: "Do these extracted requirements accurately represent what needs to be built? Any additions or corrections?"

Update the requirements based on user feedback until confirmation is received.

## CONTENT TO SAVE TO DOCUMENT:

After extraction and confirmation, update {planning_artifacts}/epics.md with:

- Complete FR list in {{fr_list}} section
- Complete NFR list in {{nfr_list}} section
- All additional requirements in {{additional_requirements}} section
- UX Design requirements in {{ux_design_requirements}} section (if UX document exists)

### 10. Present MENU OPTIONS

Display: `**Confirm the Requirements are complete and correct to [C] continue:**`

#### EXECUTION RULES:

- ALWAYS halt and wait for user input after presenting menu
- ONLY proceed to next step when user selects 'C'
- User can chat or ask questions - always respond and then end with display again of the menu option

#### Menu Handling Logic:

- IF C: Save all to {planning_artifacts}/epics.md, update frontmatter, then read fully and follow: ./step-02-design-epics.md
- IF Any other comments or queries: help user respond then [Redisplay Menu Options](#10-present-menu-options)

## CRITICAL STEP COMPLETION NOTE

ONLY WHEN C is selected and all requirements are saved to document and frontmatter is updated, will you then read fully and follow: ./step-02-design-epics.md to begin epic design step.

---

## 🚨 SYSTEM SUCCESS/FAILURE METRICS

### ✅ SUCCESS:

- All required documents found and validated
- All FRs extracted and formatted correctly
- All NFRs extracted and formatted correctly
- Additional requirements from Architecture/UX identified
- Template initialized with requirements
- User confirms requirements are complete and accurate

### ❌ SYSTEM FAILURE:

- Missing required documents
- Incomplete requirements extraction
- Template not properly initialized

**Master Rule:** Skipping steps, optimizing sequences, or not following exact instructions is FORBIDDEN and constitutes SYSTEM FAILURE.

content.content:
1	---
2	title: Cerne
3	status: final
4	created: 2026-10-25
5	updated: 2026-10-26
6	---
7	
8	# PRD: Cerne
9	
10	## 0. Document Purpose
11	
12	This PRD defines the product the Cerne Flutter app must become, built on `docs/input/requirements.md` (the frozen product specification), `docs/input/prototype/` (the frozen visual/screen reference), and `docs/input/backend/` (the frozen, already-built API contract). It also builds on three prior planning artifacts for this project — a product brief, a Working-Backwards PRFAQ, and an F000 technical-decisions forge session — without duplicating them; where those documents already settled something, this PRD states the conclusion and points back rather than re-deriving it. Implementation-level rationale (package choices, rejected alternatives, market-sizing detail, regulatory citations) lives in `addendum.md`, not here.
13	
14	The document is structured so downstream work — UX specification, architecture, and epic/story breakdown — can reference it by stable ID: Functional Requirements are numbered globally (FR-1 through FR-43) regardless of which feature section they sit in, User Journeys are numbered UJ-1 through UJ-6, and Success Metrics SM-1 onward. Terms introduced in §3 Glossary are used verbatim everywhere else in this document.
15	
16	Audience: the solo author, acting across PM/UX/architecture/dev roles for this capstone (TCC) project, and the academic reviewers who evaluate it. `[ASSUMPTION: ...]` tags mark places this PRD inferred something the source documents left unstated; see §9 for the full index.
17	
18	The single most consequential unknown for downstream sequencing: no project timeline, deadline, or defense date is stated anywhere in the source documents (§8 OQ-1).
19	
20	## 1. Vision
21	
22	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app whose AI assistant actually remembers the user. The user captures their day by text, voice, or photo; a conversational agent then answers using retrieval-augmented generation over that person's own past entries — not the stateless, generically-worded responses that dominate the AI-journaling category today. The product's bet is narrow and deliberate: not a bigger feature set than competitors, but a better memory.
23	
24	Cerne is explicitly not a mental-health or clinical tool. It makes no diagnostic claims, detects no risk signals (self-harm or suicidal ideation), and is positioned so a user processing their day through writing is never made to feel they are being monitored or clinically assessed. This is a product stance, not just a legal fence — current regulatory pressure on "AI companion" chatbots makes a non-clinical, non-companion framing a timing advantage as well as a safety one.
25	
26	Within this project's boundary, "done" means a working, fully tested iOS app that proves the RAG-memory differentiator end-to-end against the real (frozen) backend — covering capture, processing, chat, search, export, and account management — while leaving three named extension features (§5) as inert placeholders rather than attempting partial, half-working versions of them.
27	
28	## 2. Target User
29	
30	### 2.1 Jobs To Be Done
31	
32	`[ASSUMPTION: reconstructed from the product brief and PRFAQ, not stated verbatim in docs/input — confirm or replace.]`
33	
34	The target user is a Portuguese-speaking adult already in the habit of processing their day through writing or talking to an AI, frustrated that neither medium remembers them between sessions.
35	
36	- **Functional** — capture what happened today in whichever mode is fastest in the moment (typing, speaking, or photographing a physical note/receipt-like artifact), without re-explaining context the app should already have.
37	- **Emotional** — feel understood in light of one's own history, not answered with a generic response that could apply to anyone.
38	- **Social/contextual** — maintain a private record that stays private; a quiet fear this persona carries is that a personal diary could be mined, sold, or silently reinterpreted as a mental-health signal.
39	- **Explicitly not** — seeking therapy, diagnosis, or a "companion" relationship with the AI; this user would be put off by anything implying they need clinical help.
40	
41	### 2.2 Non-Users (v1)
42	
43	- Users seeking a clinical, diagnostic, or crisis-support tool — out of scope by design (§5).
44	- Users who need to edit or delete past Entries, or journal fully offline — Entries are immutable and writes are cloud-only (backend constraint; see §5, §8 OQ-5).
45	- Android users — platform is iOS, portrait-only, for this delivery.
46	- Users seeking AI-automated organization (auto-categorization, auto-extracted goals) — these exist only as static placeholders (§5).
47	
48	### 2.3 Key User Journeys
49	
50	- **UJ-1. Mara unlocks the app and captures her day before bed.**
51	  - **Persona + context:** `[ASSUMPTION]` Mara, journals most nights, phone always nearby, wants capture to take under 30 seconds.
52	  - **Entry state:** app backgrounded since this morning (>5 min), biometric vault active.
53	  - **Path:** opens app → Tela 0 splash auto-advances → Tela 0.1 Biometria prompts Face ID → succeeds → Home/Chat. Taps "+" → Insertion Modal opens on the Texto tab → she switches to Áudio, records 40 seconds → recording stops → "Processando" → on-device transcription completes → "Transcrito" text shown → taps Salvar.
54	  - **Climax:** the Entry appears, saved, with no round-trip to a server required for the transcription step itself.
55	  - **Resolution:** modal closes, she's back on Home/Chat; the Entry now exists for RF07 (timeline) and RF06 (search) to surface later.
56	  - **Edge case:** Face ID fails twice → "Usar PIN" link → Tela 0.1b/0.1c PIN flow, no lockout (FR-5).
57	
58	- **UJ-2. Mara asks the assistant about a pattern she's noticed.**
59	  - **Entry state:** authenticated, on Home/Chat, has weeks of prior entries.
60	  - **Path:** types a question referencing something she wrote about weeks ago → sends → streaming response begins, grounded in RAG over her own Entries (not a generic answer) → response completes.
61	  - **Climax:** the response correctly surfaces something specific from her own history — the core differentiator (§1) made concrete.
62	  - **Resolution:** conversation continues naturally; she can keep chatting or start a new conversation from the side menu.
63	  - **Edge case:** the stream can drop mid-response, and separately her session can expire mid-conversation — either way she can recover (retry, or "Entrar novamente") without losing the thread of what she was saying (FR-2, FR-26).
64	  - **RF08 note:** this same conversation surface is also where an Insight (RF08) can arrive unprompted, without Mara having asked for it — the mechanism realizes this journey rather than a separate one.
65	
66	- **UJ-3. Mara saves something she said in chat as a proper journal entry.**
67	  - **Entry state:** mid-conversation, has just written a reflective message of her own.
68	  - **Path:** taps the bookmark affordance on her own message (never available on the AI's replies) → saving state shown → saved.
69	  - **Climax:** the message now exists as a real Entry (source=`chat`), reachable later from the timeline and search, without her having to retype it.
70	  - **Resolution:** chat continues uninterrupted either way.
71	  - **Edge case:** tapping save twice, or a save that fails, both leave the chat fully usable and recoverable (FR-29, FR-30).
72	
73	- **UJ-4. Mara looks for everything she wrote about feeling anxious before a specific event.**
74	  - **Entry state:** on Meus Registros (timeline), has Entries from text, audio, and photo sources.
75	  - **Path:** types a word like "ansiedade" into the search bar → results return Entries that used related but different wording (e.g. "nervosismo") because the match is semantic, not literal → she narrows further with the filter sheet (date range, source) → active filters shown as removable chips.
76	  - **Climax:** she finds Entries she could not have found with exact-keyword search, from an origin (audio transcript) she'd forgotten she used.
77	  - **Resolution:** clears filters → full list restored without a screen reload.
78	  - **Edge case:** no results for the period → the screen's empty state, distinct from the "no entries at all" empty state (§4.5 FR-16), still offers a path back to capture.
79	
80	- **UJ-5. Mara exports a narrative summary of her last three months before a personal check-in with herself.**
81	  - **Entry state:** on Meus Registros, taps the download icon.
82	  - **Path:** selects a period → export sheet shows "Pendente" → "Processando" → either "Concluído" (both PDF narrative and raw data downloadable) or, if only the AI narrative step failed, raw data remains downloadable while the narrative is marked unavailable — the job is never blocked end-to-end by a narrative failure.
83	  - **Climax:** she gets a readable, honest reflection of her last three months, or at minimum her raw data, every time she asks.
84	  - **Resolution:** closes the sheet via "Fechar."
85	  - **Edge case:** she picks a period with zero Entries → "Período vazio" state, no crash, no download offered (FR-37).
86	
87	- **UJ-6. Mara checks her settings Dashboard, then eventually decides to leave.**
88	  - **Entry state:** on Configurações.
89	  - **Path:** Dashboard renders a chart + narrative computed on demand; she edits her display name inline; much later, in a separate session, she decides to stop using the app and taps "Apagar conta," confirms in the red dialog.
90	  - **Climax:** her account and data are hard-deleted, consistent with the "this is genuinely mine to remove" expectation a journaling app sets.
91	  - **Resolution:** routed back to the Biometric Vault / login screen, same as logout (no dedicated confirmation screen exists for either flow — §8 OQ-4).
92	  - **Edge case:** Dashboard has data but the AI-generated narrative specifically failed to generate — a distinct state from "zero Entries," since the chart still renders (FR-39).
93	
94	## 3. Glossary
95	
96	- **Entry** — A persisted journal record created via one of four sources: `manual` (text), `audio`, `photo`, or `chat` (via RF10). Immutable once created — no edit or delete operation exists. Always created through `POST /entries`.
97	- **Chat Session** — A persistent, named conversation thread with the AI assistant. A user may hold multiple sessions, switchable from the side menu.
98	- **Chat Message** — A single turn within a Chat Session; distinct from an Entry unless explicitly saved via RF10 (Save Chat Message as Entry).
99	- **Insertion Modal** — The bottom-sheet UI, opened from the "+" control on Home/Chat, through which all Entries are captured (Texto / Áudio / Foto tabs).
100	- **Sync Badge** — A per-Entry UI indicator with exactly three states: *Synchronizing*, *Synchronization error*, *Synchronized*. Derived entirely client-side from `Entry.updatedAt` and `Entry.serverRevision`; the backend has no `sync_status` field.
101	- **Insight** — An AI-generated message the assistant injects into a Chat Session unprompted, per RF08's trigger conditions.
102	- **Export Job** — An asynchronous job (RF05) producing a narrative PDF and/or raw-data download for a date period; tracked by independent `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) fields.
103	- **Dashboard** — The evolution chart + narrative text on the Configurações screen (RF09), computed on demand when the screen opens.
104	- **Biometric Vault** — The RF03 access barrier (Face ID / Touch ID / PIN) gating the whole app, validated on-device; has no backend counterpart beyond a stored preference.
105	- **Extension feature** `[ext]` — A feature named in requirements.md §2 as explicitly out of scope for this delivery; its UI exists only as an inert placeholder (§5).
106	- **Failure contract** — The `{ code, message, retryable }` shape returned by every backend error (13 closed codes; see §Cross-Cutting NFRs), consumed by every repository as `Either<Failure, T>`.
107	
108	## Information Architecture
109	
110	- **Entrance/auth surfaces:** Splash (auto-advance) → Biometric Vault (Face ID/Touch ID, PIN fallback) → Login/Signup (single screen, toggled).
111	- **Home/Chat** is the base authenticated surface, with three overlays that can appear on top of it without navigating away: the Sessão Expirada overlay (FR-2), an offline banner (FR-27), and the Insertion Modal (§4.3). The side menu (☰), opened from here, leads to Chat Session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, and Planos de Ação `[ext]`.
112	- **Meus Registros (timeline)** carries its own overlay: the Export sheet (§4.10), plus an inline filter sheet and search bar (§4.6).
113	- **Configurações** hosts the dashboard (§4.11), inline profile editing, and the account-deletion confirmation dialog (§8 OQ-4).
114	
115	## 4. Features
116	
117	*Where an FR's testable condition is a single, self-evident clause, it is folded into the FR's statement itself rather than broken out into a separate Consequences block; the separate block is used once an FR needs more than one distinct, checkable condition.*
118	
119	### 4.1 Foundation & Session Management
120	
121	**Description:** The scaffold every other feature depends on: an authenticated-session lifecycle, the app shell and base navigation, and the one cross-cutting overlay — the Sessão Expirada overlay — that can interrupt any screen. Delivered first (F000) because every unit after it assumes these exist. Realizes UJ-1, UJ-2 (edge case).
122	
123	#### FR-1: Account creation and authentication
124	
125	A user can create an account and log in with email/password, and the app can silently refresh or verify the session without forcing a re-login on every app open.
126	
127	**Consequences (testable):**
128	- Signup, login, refresh, and session-check each round-trip through their respective backend operations and surface the Failure contract on error.
129	- A valid, unexpired session persists across app restarts without re-prompting for credentials.
130	- `[ASSUMPTION]` Signup collects email + password only, matching the single-screen toggle shown in the prototype (no password-confirmation or display-name field) — see §8 OQ-2.
131	
132	#### FR-2: Expired-session recovery overlay
133	
134	When the backend reports an expired session, the app shows a "Sessão expirada" overlay on top of the current screen rather than navigating away from it.
135	
136	**Consequences (testable):**
137	- The screen underneath (including scroll position and in-progress state, e.g. an open chat) is preserved while the overlay is shown.
138	- "Entrar novamente" routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow (RF03), not a full logout-and-login form.
139	- The overlay can appear while viewing the timeline (RF07, called out explicitly in requirements.md as session-dependent) or chat (RF04, shown as the "Sessão expirada" state in `prototype-extract.md`).
140	
141	#### FR-3: Base navigation shell
142	
143	The app provides navigation between Home/Chat, the side menu, Meus Registros, and Configurações, with clearly marked placeholders for RF01–RF10 functionality not yet built in this unit.
144	
145	**Consequences (testable):**
146	- All four surfaces are reachable from app launch without requiring any RF01–RF10 feature to be implemented.
147	- Placeholders are visually distinguishable from finished screens (no silent dead ends that look complete).
148	
149	---
150	
151	### 4.2 Biometric Authentication Vault (RF03)
152	
153	**Description:** A device-validated access barrier in front of all user data. Realizes UJ-1 (entry + edge case).
154	
155	#### FR-4: App-access gate
156	
157	The app requires Face ID, Touch ID, or PIN before showing any user data, on cold start and after the idle timeout (FR-6).
158	
159	**Consequences (testable):**
160	- No screen other than the vault/login screen is reachable before authentication succeeds.
161	- No biometric data or biometric call ever reaches the backend — validation is 100% on-device.
162	
163	#### FR-5: Biometric-failure fallback to PIN
164	
165	A failed biometric attempt offers PIN entry as an alternative and never locks the user out of their own app.
166	
167	**Consequences (testable):**
168	- After a biometric failure, a PIN entry path is always reachable (Tela 0.1c).
169	- Repeated biometric failures that trigger an OS-level lockout are detected and routed to the app's own PIN fallback rather than retried against the OS.
170	
171	#### FR-6: Fixed idle re-authentication timeout
172	
173	Returning to the app from the background after 5 minutes requires re-authentication; this value is fixed, not user-configurable.
174	
175	**Consequences (testable):**
176	- Resuming before 5 minutes elapsed does not prompt re-authentication.
177	- Resuming after 5 minutes always prompts re-authentication, regardless of any user setting.
178	
179	#### FR-7: Biometric preference persistence
180	
181	The user's choice to enable/disable biometric gating is saved server-side via `PATCH /account/settings` and survives both app restarts and reinstalls, since the value is fetched from the account, not cached only on-device.
182	
183	**Consequences (testable):**
184	- Disabling biometrics still leaves PIN as the access method — the vault itself cannot be turned off entirely.
185	
186	---
187	
188	### 4.3 Multimodal Capture (RF01)
189	
190	**Description:** The single entry point for creating a journal Entry, in text, audio, or photo form, all through the Insertion Modal. Realizes UJ-1.
191	
192	#### FR-8: Text Entry capture
193	
194	A user can type free text in the Insertion Modal and save it as an Entry (source=`manual`).
195	
196	#### FR-9: Audio Entry capture
197	
198	A user can record audio in the Insertion Modal; the raw recording becomes the basis of an Entry (source=`audio`) once processed (RF02).
199	
200	#### FR-10: Photo Entry capture
201	
202	A user can capture or select a photo in the Insertion Modal; it becomes the basis of an Entry (source=`photo`) once processed (RF02).
203	
204	**Consequences (testable, FR-8 through FR-10):**
205	- All three modalities produce the same persisted Entry shape — none is structurally special-cased after capture.
206	- Each call to `POST /entries` carries the correct `source` value for its modality.
207	
208	#### FR-11: Cancel-safe capture
209	
210	Interrupting a capture in progress (e.g., stopping a recording before saving, backing out mid-photo) never creates a partial or empty Entry.
211	
212	**Consequences (testable):**
213	- No `POST /entries` call fires for an abandoned capture.
214	- `[OPEN]` Switching tabs mid-recording (e.g. Áudio → Foto) is undefined behavior in the current prototype — see §8 OQ-3.
215	
216	---
217	
218	### 4.4 Speech-to-Text / OCR Processing (RF02)
219	
220	**Description:** Turns raw audio into text on-device, and raw photos into text via the backend, before an Entry is persisted. Realizes UJ-1.
221	
222	#### FR-12: On-device audio transcription
223	
224	Recorded audio is transcribed to text entirely on-device via `whisper_ggml`; the audio file itself is never sent to the backend.
225	
226	**Consequences (testable):**
227	- Exactly four visible states occur in sequence or on failure: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry, media never discarded.
228	- No network call containing audio bytes is made at any point in this pipeline.
229	
230	#### FR-13: Backend OCR for photos
231	
232	A captured photo is sent to `POST /media/ocr` to extract text before the Entry is created.
233	
234	**Consequences (testable):**
235	- Mirrors FR-12's four-state pattern: capture → processing OCR → recognized → (on failure) error with retry, photo never discarded.
236	- On OCR failure, the user has two recovery paths, not one: retry the OCR step, or save the Entry with no extracted text ("Salvar só a foto") — both are shown in the prototype's OCR-failure state.
237	- `OCR_NO_TEXT` (no extractable text found) is handled as a distinct, user-visible outcome, not a generic failure.
238	
239	**Notes:** Test material for both pipelines — sample audio, OCR test images, and expected transcription output — lives in `docs/input/backend/fixtures/`.
240	
241	---
242	
243	### 4.5 Multi-Source History / Timeline (RF07)
244	
245	**Description:** A chronological view of every Entry regardless of origin, each carrying a Sync Badge. Realizes UJ-1 (as the destination for captured entries) and UJ-4 (as the surface search/filter operates on).
246	
247	#### FR-14: Chronological Entry list
248	
249	All Entries, from any source, are listed together grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.
250	
251	#### FR-15: Per-entry Sync Badge
252	
253	Each Entry shows one of three Sync Badge states, derived client-side from `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` and local pending-write state — the backend exposes no `sync_status` field.
254	
255	**Consequences (testable):**
256	- A freshly created Entry shows "Synchronizing" until the server's write confirmation is reconciled, then "Synchronized."
257	- A write that fails (network or any Failure-contract code) shows "Synchronization error" until a subsequent successful write reconciles it.
258	- The badge's update stream runs independently of the auth/session stream — a pending sync-badge transition is never blocked, delayed, or cleared by session-expiry handling (FR-17).
259	- `[OPEN]` No retry affordance is visible on the error state in the current prototype — see §8 OQ-6.
260	
261	#### FR-16: Empty-state handling
262	
263	With zero Entries, the screen shows a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture, not a blank list.
264	
265	#### FR-17: Session-expiry resilience mid-view
266	
267	If the session expires while viewing the timeline, the FR-2 overlay appears without crashing or losing scroll position.
268	
269	#### FR-18: Entry detail view
270	
271	A user can open a single Entry from the timeline to see its full content, via `GET /entries/:id`.
272	
273	**Consequences (testable):**
274	- Opening an Entry never mutates it — there is no edit affordance, consistent with Entries being immutable (§3 Glossary).
275	- A detail request for an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user returns `NOT_FOUND` (RNF04), not a permission-denied code.
276	
277	**Feature-specific NFRs:** No BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly — the three streams this screen composes (auth status, Sync Badge state, and Entry data) combine only through the domain layer, never via a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.
278	
279	---
280	
281	### 4.6 Semantic Search / Filter (RF06)
282	
283	**Description:** Meaning-based search plus metadata filters over the timeline from §4.5. Realizes UJ-4.
284	
285	#### FR-19: Semantic search
286	
287	A user can search Entries by meaning, not just literal keyword match (e.g. "ansiedade" matches an entry that only used "nervosismo"), via `GET /entries/search`.
288	
289	#### FR-20: Metadata filters
290	
291	A user can filter by source and date range (`dateFrom`/`dateTo`); no tag/category filter exists, since categorization is an extension feature (§5). Filtering with no active search term queries `GET /entries`; filtering combined with an active search term queries `GET /entries/search`, carrying the same filter parameters.
292	
293	**Consequences (testable, FR-19/FR-20):**
294	- Multiple active filters combine with AND semantics.
295	- `[OPEN]` How an active text search and active filters interact when both are set simultaneously is unspecified in the prototype — see §8 OQ-7.
296	
297	#### FR-21: Debounced search input
298	
299	Search input is debounced by 300ms before firing a request.
300	
301	#### FR-22: Non-disruptive filter clearing
302	
303	Clearing active filters restores the full list in place, without a full screen reload, and the cache stays duplicate-free after a reconnect (cloud-only; offline is view-only for this screen).
304	
305	**Notes:** Test material (a seeded set of entries with known semantic relationships, for verifying true meaning-based matches) lives in `docs/input/backend/fixtures/seeded-search-entries.md`.
306	
307	---
308	
309	### 4.7 Interactive Chat with Memory / RAG (RF04)
310	
311	**Description:** The core differentiator (§1): a persistent, multi-session conversation where the assistant answers using RAG over the user's own Entries. Realizes UJ-2.
312	
313	#### FR-23: Send message, receive RAG-grounded streaming response
314	
315	A user sends a Chat Message and receives a streamed response grounded in semantic retrieval over their own Entries, via SSE on `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`.
316	
317	**Consequences (testable):**
318	- Exactly three visible states exist: streaming/processing, error, complete.
319	- Chat Messages never automatically create Entries — RF10 is the sole, explicit exception.
320	
321	#### FR-24: Multi-session chat history
322	
323	A user can hold multiple named Chat Sessions, listed and switchable from the side menu.
324	
325	#### FR-25: New-conversation action
326	
327	A user can start a new Chat Session from the side menu.
328	
329	**Consequences (testable):**
330	- `POST /chat/sessions` is blocked offline — starting a new Chat Session requires connectivity, consistent with the offline composer lock on existing conversations (FR-27).
331	
332	#### FR-26: Dropped-stream resilience
333	
334	If a response stream drops mid-generation, the partial message stays on screen with a failure indicator; the user can retry via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry`, which regenerates without duplicating the original question.
335	
336	#### FR-27: Offline composer lock
337	
338	When offline, the message composer is disabled while the existing conversation history remains visible and navigable.
339	
340	---
341	
342	### 4.8 Save Chat Message as Entry (RF10)
343	
344	**Description:** Lets a user turn their own Chat Message into a real Entry. Realizes UJ-3. Depends on RF01 and RF04.
345	
346	#### FR-28: Bookmark a user message into an Entry
347	
348	A "save" affordance appears only on the user's own Chat Messages (never on AI responses) and, when used, creates an Entry (source=`chat`, carrying `chatMessageId`) through the same shared entries use case RF01 defines — never by importing the entries repository or data source directly (RNF06).
349	
350	#### FR-29: Idempotent save
351	
352	Saving the same Chat Message more than once does not create a duplicate Entry and never surfaces a conflict error (the backend returns 200, not 409).
353	
354	#### FR-30: Save-failure isolation
355	
356	If the save fails, the surrounding Chat Session remains fully usable, and the save affordance resets to a retryable state rather than freezing.
357	
358	---
359	
360	### 4.9 Proactive Insights (RF08)
361	
362	**Description:** The mechanism by which the assistant injects an unprompted suggestion into the conversation. Scope is the trigger/injection mechanism only — the quality of the generated Insight text is explicitly out of scope for acceptance testing. Realizes UJ-2 (the unprompted-Insight moment within an ongoing conversation). Depends on RF04.
363	
364	#### FR-31: Unprompted Insight injection
365	
366	An Insight is injected into the active Chat Session once per satisfied condition — triggered by either 5 user messages sent or 2 minutes of inactivity, whichever occurs first — via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight`.
367	
368	#### FR-32: Insight failure isolation
369	
370	A failure to generate an Insight does not interrupt or break the main chat experience.
371	
372	**Consequences (testable):**
373	- The message composer remains enabled and no error overlay appears over the conversation when Insight generation fails.
374	- The user can keep sending and receiving ordinary Chat Messages (FR-23) uninterrupted; only the Insight itself is absent.
375	
376	#### FR-33: Non-disruptive dismissal
377	
378	Dismissing an Insight does not affect scroll position or any other conversation state.
379	
380	---
381	
382	### 4.10 Personal Summary Export (RF05)
383	
384	**Description:** On-demand generation of a narrative PDF summary plus an always-available raw-data download. Scope is job/file/failure handling only — the quality of the generated narrative text is explicitly out of scope for acceptance testing. Realizes UJ-5. Depends on RF07.
385	
386	#### FR-34: Request a period export
387	
388	A user can request an export for a chosen date period via `POST /export/summary`.
389	
390	#### FR-35: Job status across five screen states
391	
392	The export sheet reflects the job's progress across five states — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio — via `GET /export/:jobId/status`, which reports `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) independently.
393	
394	#### FR-36: Narrative-independent raw-data download
395	
396	Raw data is downloadable via `GET /export/:jobId/download` as soon as it's ready, even if the AI narrative step is still processing, has failed, or was skipped — the narrative never blocks the data download.
397	
398	#### FR-37: Empty-period handling
399	
400	Requesting an export for a period with zero Entries surfaces "Período vazio" with no download offered and no crash.
401	
402	---
403	
404	### 4.11 Temporal Summaries / Dashboard & Account (RF09)
405	
406	**Description:** The Configurações screen's evolution Dashboard, plus the profile and account actions that live there. Scope for the Dashboard is aggregation/rendering only — AI narrative text quality is explicitly out of scope for acceptance testing. Realizes UJ-6. Depends on F000, RF01.
407	
408	#### FR-38: On-demand dashboard aggregation
409	
410	Opening Configurações computes and renders an evolution chart via `GET /dashboard/aggregate`, correctly at zero, one, and more-than-thirty Entries.
411	
412	#### FR-39: Independent narrative text
413	
414	A separate narrative text is fetched via `GET /dashboard/narrative`; its failure is a distinct, chart-still-renders state, never blocking the chart (two independent endpoints by design).
415	
416	#### FR-40: Cache invalidation on new Entry
417	
418	The dashboard's aggregation recalculates after a new Entry is created elsewhere in the app; since Entries are immutable, invalidation only ever needs to trigger on create, never on edit.
419	
420	#### FR-41: Profile name editing
421	
422	A user can edit their display name inline on Configurações via `PATCH /account/settings`.
423	
424	#### FR-42: Logout
425	
426	"Sair" ends the session (`POST /auth/logout`) and returns to the Biometric Vault / login screen.
427	
428	#### FR-43: Account deletion
429	
430	"Apagar conta" shows a confirmation dialog; on confirmation, the account and all associated data are hard-deleted (`DELETE /account`, LGPD-driven), and the user is routed to the same destination as logout.
431	
432	**Notes:** `[NOTE FOR PM]` No dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists in the current prototype (§8 OQ-4) — revisit if post-defense polish time exists.
433	
434	## 5. Non-Goals (Explicit)
435	
436	- **Dynamic AI categorization of Entries** `[ext]` — downgraded to manual, user-created tags on Meus Registros; no AI logic behind it.
437	- **Autonomous AI goal extraction** `[ext]` — exists only as a static Action Plans Kanban screen with no underlying logic.
438	- **Dynamic AI persona adjustment** `[ext]` — exists only as a cosmetic Settings selector (Analítico/Empático/Socrático) that does not change assistant behavior in this delivery.
439	- **Any risk-signal detection** (self-harm, suicidal ideation) — a deliberate scope exclusion tied to the product's non-clinical stance (§1), not an oversight. A low-cost static crisis-resources disclaimer is a candidate fast-follow, not committed (§8 OQ-8).
440	- **Entry editing or deletion** — no such backend operation exists; Entries are permanent once created.
441	- **Offline Entry creation** — all writes are cloud-only; offline mode is view-only for already-synced data.
442	- **Android, or any platform beyond iOS portrait** for this delivery.
443	- **Any change to the backend, its contract, or its configuration** — consumed exactly as documented.
444	- **Any direct call to an AI provider (Claude, Voyage AI) from the app** — every AI-touching operation goes through the backend.
445	- **Grading or verifying the quality of AI-generated text** (Insights, export narratives, dashboard narrative) — RF05/RF08/RF09 are scoped to mechanism, failure-handling, and UI-safety only; generated-content quality is explicitly out of acceptance scope per requirements.md. (RF04's chat responses and RF06's search-result relevance carry no such explicit exclusion in requirements.md — see §8 OQ-10.)
446	
447	## 6. MVP Scope
448	
449	### 6.1 In Scope
450	
451	- F000 (Foundation) → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09, in that order (requirements.md §12).
452	- All 43 FRs in §4, plus the feature-specific NFRs called out alongside them, to their stated acceptance criteria.
453	
454	### 6.2 Out of Scope for MVP
455	
456	- Everything listed in §5.
457	- Any feature reordering outside the delivery sequence in §6.1 — later units assume earlier ones exist (e.g. RF10 assumes RF01 and RF04 are both done).
458	
459	## 7. Success Metrics
460	
461	*This is an academic capstone with no customer-acquisition or adoption target; success is defined by specification conformance, not usage.* Stated plainly: this PRD's graded metrics (SM-1–3) can only confirm the RAG-memory mechanism is wired correctly end-to-end — whether the memory bet (§1) actually pays off for a real user is not a graded surface for this delivery (SM-5 is deliberately informal and uninstrumented; see also §8 OQ-10).
462	
463	**Primary**
464	- **SM-1**: Every acceptance criterion stated per-RF in requirements.md §1 passes. Validates FR-1 through FR-43, the feature-specific NFRs called out in §4 (e.g. the BLoC-composition rule under §4.5 FR-18), and RNF01's performance thresholds (manual timing spot-check per module, not automated).
465	- **SM-2**: Zero Clean Architecture layer violations (RNF06) and ≥80% domain-layer test coverage (RNF07), verified across all 11 feature modules.
466	- **SM-3**: All 15 required network-failure scenarios (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types) are handled per the Failure contract, with zero unhandled exceptions (RNF09).
467	
468	**Secondary**
469	- **SM-4**: Zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart` (RNF08), verified by inspection.
470	- **SM-5** *(qualitative, informal)*: the assistant surfaces something true from weeks earlier without being asked to, and the act of writing starts to feel worth repeating. No instrumentation planned to measure this for v1 — it is a design intent, not a graded criterion.
471	
472	**Counter-metrics (do not optimize)**
473	- **SM-C1**: Scope creep into AI-generated content *quality* work (better prompts, better narratives) — explicitly out of grading scope (§5) and would divert effort from the mechanism work that is actually graded. Counterbalances SM-1.
474	- **SM-C2**: Test coverage inflated with trivial/tautological tests to hit the RNF07 80% number — the metric is domain-layer correctness, not a percentage. Counterbalances SM-2.
475	
476	## 8. Open Questions
477	
478	1. **No project timeline, deadline, or defense date is stated anywhere in the source documents.** This blocks any confident sequencing/pacing judgment for downstream epics work. *(Flagged by the PRFAQ distillate as the single biggest open input.)*
479	2. **Signup field set is underspecified.** The prototype shows one screen toggled between Entrar/Criar conta with only email+password fields visible — no password confirmation, no display-name capture at signup. Confirm this is intentional before building FR-1. *(blocks F000 — build unit 1 of 11)*
480	3. **Tab-switching mid-capture in the Insertion Modal is undefined** (e.g., switching from Áudio to Foto while a recording is in progress) — decide: discard, warn, or persist the in-progress capture (affects FR-11). *(blocks RF01 — build unit 3 of 11)*
481	4. **No "account deleted" or "signed out" confirmation screen exists** — both flows dead-end at the Biometric Vault screen. Decide whether this is acceptable for v1 or needs even a lightweight confirmation (affects FR-42/FR-43). *(blocks RF09 — build unit 11 of 11; lowest urgency of the sequenced OQs)*
482	5. **(Already resolved, kept here only for visibility — not a live open question.)** Cloud-only, immutable-entry design is a backend constraint, not a product choice: there is no appetite to request a contract change (confirmed — none per `AGENTS.md`); recorded so it isn't silently re-discovered as a "bug" later.
483	6. **The Sync Badge error state has no visible retry affordance in the current prototype** — decide whether the badge needs one, or whether reconciliation on the next successful write is sufficient (affects FR-15). *(blocks RF07 — build unit 5 of 11)*
484	7. **Combined search + filter behavior is unspecified** — when both a search term and active filters are set, decide the intended interaction (AND-combine vs. one overriding the other) (affects FR-19/FR-20). *(blocks RF06 — build unit 6 of 11)*
485	8. **A static, no-logic crisis-resources disclaimer was recommended (PRFAQ) as a low-cost way to close the "silent gap" left by having no risk-signal detection**, without contradicting the non-clinical stance (§1, §5). Not yet decided for inclusion.
486	9. **Whether Cerne continues as a maintained portfolio piece after the defense, or ends as a one-time academic artifact**, is unresolved and would change how much polish-time investment in OQ-2/OQ-4/OQ-6/OQ-7 is worth it.
487	10. **Whether RF04's chat-response quality, and separately RF06's search-result quality, should carry the same "mechanism only, never graded" boundary that requirements.md states explicitly for RF05/RF08/RF09 is unstated for both.** Treated here as a genuine gap for each, not silently extended or silently dropped (§5, §Constraints and Guardrails). *(blocks grading boundary for RF04 — build unit 7 of 11 — and RF06 — build unit 6 of 11)*
488	11. **"Cerne" is a working title** — confirm or replace.
489	
490	## 9. Assumptions Index
491	
492	- §2.1/§2.3 — The target-user persona (functional/emotional/social JTBD, the "Mara" journeys) is reconstructed from the product brief and PRFAQ, not stated verbatim in `docs/input/`.
493	- §4.1 FR-1 — Signup is assumed to collect only email + password (see OQ-2 for the decision this depends on).
494	
495	## Cross-Cutting NFRs
496	
497	- **RNF01 (performance):** Local UI interactions respond in <100ms; any network call taking >300ms shows a loading indicator. Verified via manual timing spot-checks during each feature module's QA pass (SM-1) — no automated performance instrumentation is planned for this delivery.
498	- **RNF02 (PII handling)** `[inherited, not verified by this delivery]`: PII stripping runs via a Claude Haiku 4.5 structured prompt/tool-use step (not a dedicated NER model), server-side only.
499	- **RNF03 (data retention)** `[inherited, not verified by this delivery]`: Zero data retention by upstream AI providers.
500	- **RNF04 (data isolation):** Row Level Security (Supabase) enforces per-user data isolation; the client never needs its own authorization logic for cross-user access — the backend uniformly returns `NOT_FOUND` (never a permission-denied code) for any resource that doesn't belong to the requesting user, so existence of other users' data is never revealed.
501	- **RNF05 (account deletion):** Hard delete of account and all associated data on request (LGPD).
502	- **RNF06 (architecture):** Zero Clean Architecture layer violations — the domain layer imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything from a `data/` layer, in any of the 11 feature modules.
503	- **RNF07 (test coverage):** ≥80% domain-layer test coverage.
504	- **RNF08 (visual fidelity):** Visual fidelity to the prototype (color, typography, spacing); zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`.
505	- **RNF09 (resilience):** Every repository returns `Either<Failure, T>`; 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types (timeout, malformed response, no connection) = 15 tested failure scenarios, zero unhandled exceptions.
506	
507	**The Failure contract** — every backend error has the shape `{ code, message, retryable }`, drawn from a closed set of 13 codes (the one extra client-only case, a malformed/unparseable response, is handled identically but never retryable):
508	
509	| Code | Retryable | Meaning |
510	|---|---|---|
511	| AUTH_EXPIRED | no | access token expired — triggers the FR-2 overlay |
512	| AUTH_INVALID | no | invalid credentials (password login only — never originates from biometrics, since biometric validation is on-device) |
513	| NETWORK_TIMEOUT | yes | request timed out |
514	| NETWORK_OFFLINE | yes | connection ended with no HTTP response at all — must be handled as a distinct "no response received" branch, not dispatched on a status code |
515	| VALIDATION_ERROR | no | malformed request payload |
516	| PII_CHECK_FAILED | yes | server-side PII scan step failed |
517	| EMBEDDING_FAILED | yes | embedding generation failed |
518	| AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT | yes | AI generation step timed out |
519	| NOT_FOUND | no | resource missing, or belongs to another user (RNF04) |
520	| RATE_LIMITED | yes | too many requests |
521	| EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD | no | export requested for a period with no Entries (FR-37) |
522	| PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE | no | upload exceeds size limit |
523	| OCR_NO_TEXT | no | OCR found no extractable text (FR-13) |
524	
525	## Constraints and Guardrails
526	
527	Privacy, safety, and platform constraints are stated once each, at the FR/NFR/Non-Goal that owns them, rather than restated here. Index:
528	
529	- **Privacy** — on-device-only audio and biometrics (FR-12, FR-4), zero AI-provider data retention (RNF03), server-side PII stripping (RNF02), RLS-enforced data isolation (RNF04).
530	- **Safety** — non-clinical framing and no risk-signal detection (§1, §5), the mechanism-only AI-content-quality boundary and its two open exceptions, RF04 and RF06 (§5, §8 OQ-10).
531	- **Platform** — iOS portrait-only, frozen backend contract, no direct AI-provider calls from the app (§5).
532	
533	## Aesthetic and Tone
534	
535	The prototype (`docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §3) defines a named visual token system — color, typography, spacing, radii, elevation, and iconography — that `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` must be the single source of truth for; no visual value may appear hardcoded anywhere else in the app (RNF08). Interface copy throughout the product is in Brazilian Portuguese. Tone follows directly from §1's stance: reflective and private, never clinical, never styled as a "companion" the user is meant to bond with.
536	
537	---
538	*Addendum: `addendum.md` in this folder holds implementation-level decisions (routing, HTTP client, local cache, DI, package choices and rejected alternatives), competitive-landscape and market-sizing detail, regulatory citations, and corrections-carried-forward from prior planning sessions — none of it duplicated here.*
539

# PRD: Cerne

## 0. Document Purpose

This PRD defines the product the Cerne Flutter app must become, built on `docs/input/requirements.md` (the frozen product specification), `docs/input/prototype/` (the frozen visual/screen reference), and `docs/input/backend/` (the frozen, already-built API contract). It also builds on three prior planning artifacts for this project — a product brief, a Working-Backwards PRFAQ, and an F000 technical-decisions forge session — without duplicating them; where those documents already settled something, this PRD states the conclusion and points back rather than re-deriving it. Implementation-level rationale (package choices, rejected alternatives, market-sizing detail, regulatory citations) lives in `addendum.md`, not here.

The document is structured so downstream work — UX specification, architecture, and epic/story breakdown — can reference it by stable ID: Functional Requirements are numbered globally (FR-1 through FR-43) regardless of which feature section they sit in, User Journeys are numbered UJ-1 through UJ-6, and Success Metrics SM-1 onward. Terms introduced in §3 Glossary are used verbatim everywhere else in this document.

## 1. Vision

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app whose AI assistant actually remembers the user. The user captures their day by text, voice, or photo; a conversational agent then answers using retrieval-augmented generation over that person's own past entries — not the stateless, generically-worded responses that dominate the AI-journaling category today. The product's bet is narrow and deliberate: not a bigger feature set than competitors, but a better memory.

Cerne is explicitly not a mental-health or clinical tool. It makes no diagnostic claims, detects no risk signals (self-harm or suicidal ideation), and is positioned so a user processing their day through writing is never made to feel they are being monitored or clinically assessed. This is a product stance, not just a legal fence — current regulatory pressure on "AI companion" chatbots makes a non-clinical, non-companion framing a timing advantage as well as a safety one.

Within this project's boundary, "done" means a working, fully tested iOS app that proves the RAG-memory differentiator end-to-end against the real (frozen) backend — covering capture, processing, chat, search, export, and account management — while leaving three named extension features (§5) as inert placeholders rather than attempting partial, half-working versions of them.

## 2. Target User

### 2.1 Jobs To Be Done

`[ASSUMPTION: reconstructed from the product brief and PRFAQ, not stated verbatim in docs/input — confirm or replace.]`

The target user is a Portuguese-speaking adult already in the habit of processing their day through writing or talking to an AI, frustrated that neither medium remembers them between sessions.

- **Functional** — capture what happened today in whichever mode is fastest in the moment (typing, speaking, or photographing a physical note/receipt-like artifact), without re-explaining context the app should already have.
- **Emotional** — feel understood in light of one's own history, not answered with a generic response that could apply to anyone.
- **Social/contextual** — maintain a private record that stays private; a quiet fear this persona carries is that a personal diary could be mined, sold, or silently reinterpreted as a mental-health signal.
- **Explicitly not** — seeking therapy, diagnosis, or a "companion" relationship with the AI; this user would be put off by anything implying they need clinical help.

### 2.2 Non-Users (v1)

- Users seeking a clinical, diagnostic, or crisis-support tool — out of scope by design (§5).
- Users who need to edit or delete past Entries, or journal fully offline — Entries are immutable and writes are cloud-only (backend constraint; see §5, §8 OQ-5).
- Android users — platform is iOS, portrait-only, for this delivery.
- Users seeking AI-automated organization (auto-categorization, auto-extracted goals) — these exist only as static placeholders (§5).

### 2.3 Key User Journeys

- **UJ-1. Mara unlocks the app and captures her day before bed.**
  - **Persona + context:** `[ASSUMPTION]` Mara, journals most nights, phone always nearby, wants capture to take under 30 seconds.
  - **Entry state:** app backgrounded since this morning (>5 min), biometric vault active.
  - **Path:** opens app → Tela 0 splash auto-advances → Tela 0.1 Biometria prompts Face ID → succeeds → Home/Chat. Taps "+" → Insertion Modal opens on the Texto tab → she switches to Áudio, records 40 seconds → recording stops → "Processando" → on-device transcription completes → "Transcrito" text shown → taps Salvar.
  - **Climax:** the Entry appears, saved, with no round-trip to a server required for the transcription step itself.
  - **Resolution:** modal closes, she's back on Home/Chat; the Entry now exists for RF07 (timeline) and RF06 (search) to surface later.
  - **Edge case:** Face ID fails twice → "Usar PIN" link → Tela 0.1b/0.1c PIN flow, no lockout (FR-5).

- **UJ-2. Mara asks the assistant about a pattern she's noticed.**
  - **Entry state:** authenticated, on Home/Chat, has weeks of prior entries.
  - **Path:** types a question referencing something she wrote about weeks ago → sends → streaming response begins, grounded in RAG over her own Entries (not a generic answer) → response completes.
  - **Climax:** the response correctly surfaces something specific from her own history — the core differentiator (§1) made concrete.
  - **Resolution:** conversation continues naturally; she can keep chatting or start a new conversation from the side menu.
  - **Edge case:** the stream can drop mid-response, and separately her session can expire mid-conversation — either way she can recover (retry, or "Entrar novamente") without losing the thread of what she was saying (FR-2, FR-26).
  - **RF08 note:** this same conversation surface is also where an Insight (RF08) can arrive unprompted, without Mara having asked for it — the mechanism realizes this journey rather than a separate one.

- **UJ-3. Mara saves something she said in chat as a proper journal entry.**
  - **Entry state:** mid-conversation, has just written a reflective message of her own.
  - **Path:** taps the bookmark affordance on her own message (never available on the AI's replies) → saving state shown → saved.
  - **Climax:** the message now exists as a real Entry (source=`chat`), reachable later from the timeline and search, without her having to retype it.
  - **Resolution:** chat continues uninterrupted either way.
  - **Edge case:** tapping save twice, or a save that fails, both leave the chat fully usable and recoverable (FR-29, FR-30).

- **UJ-4. Mara looks for everything she wrote about feeling anxious before a specific event.**
  - **Entry state:** on Meus Registros (timeline), has Entries from text, audio, and photo sources.
  - **Path:** types a word like "ansiedade" into the search bar → results return Entries that used related but different wording (e.g. "nervosismo") because the match is semantic, not literal → she narrows further with the filter sheet (date range, source) → active filters shown as removable chips.
  - **Climax:** she finds Entries she could not have found with exact-keyword search, from an origin (audio transcript) she'd forgotten she used.
  - **Resolution:** clears filters → full list restored without a screen reload.
  - **Edge case:** no results for the period → the screen's empty state, distinct from the "no entries at all" empty state (§4.5 FR-16), still offers a path back to capture.

- **UJ-5. Mara exports a narrative summary of her last three months before a personal check-in with herself.**
  - **Entry state:** on Meus Registros, taps the download icon.
  - **Path:** selects a period → export sheet shows "Pendente" → "Processando" → either "Concluído" (both PDF narrative and raw data downloadable) or, if only the AI narrative step failed, raw data remains downloadable while the narrative is marked unavailable — the job is never blocked end-to-end by a narrative failure.
  - **Climax:** she gets a readable, honest reflection of her last three months, or at minimum her raw data, every time she asks.
  - **Resolution:** closes the sheet via "Fechar."
  - **Edge case:** she picks a period with zero Entries → "Período vazio" state, no crash, no download offered (FR-37).

- **UJ-6. Mara checks her settings Dashboard, then eventually decides to leave.**
  - **Entry state:** on Configurações.
  - **Path:** Dashboard renders a chart + narrative computed on demand; she edits her display name inline; much later, in a separate session, she decides to stop using the app and taps "Apagar conta," confirms in the red dialog.
  - **Climax:** her account and data are hard-deleted, consistent with the "this is genuinely mine to remove" expectation a journaling app sets.
  - **Resolution:** routed back to the Biometric Vault / login screen, same as logout (no dedicated confirmation screen exists for either flow — §8 OQ-4).
  - **Edge case:** Dashboard has data but the AI-generated narrative specifically failed to generate — a distinct state from "zero Entries," since the chart still renders (FR-39).

## 3. Glossary

- **Entry** — A persisted journal record created via one of four sources: `manual` (text), `audio`, `photo`, or `chat` (via RF10). Immutable once created — no edit or delete operation exists. Always created through `POST /entries`.
- **Chat Session** — A persistent, named conversation thread with the AI assistant. A user may hold multiple sessions, switchable from the side menu.
- **Chat Message** — A single turn within a Chat Session; distinct from an Entry unless explicitly saved via RF10 (Save Chat Message as Entry).
- **Insertion Modal** — The bottom-sheet UI, opened from the "+" control on Home/Chat, through which all Entries are captured (Texto / Áudio / Foto tabs).
- **Sync Badge** — A per-Entry UI indicator with exactly three states: *Synchronizing*, *Synchronization error*, *Synchronized*. Derived entirely client-side from `Entry.updatedAt` and `Entry.serverRevision`; the backend has no `sync_status` field.
- **Insight** — An AI-generated message the assistant injects into a Chat Session unprompted, per RF08's trigger conditions.
- **Export Job** — An asynchronous job (RF05) producing a narrative PDF and/or raw-data download for a date period; tracked by independent `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) fields.
- **Dashboard** — The evolution chart + narrative text on the Configurações screen (RF09), computed on demand when the screen opens.
- **Biometric Vault** — The RF03 access barrier (Face ID / Touch ID / PIN) gating the whole app, validated on-device; has no backend counterpart beyond a stored preference.
- **Extension feature** `[ext]` — A feature named in requirements.md §2 as explicitly out of scope for this delivery; its UI exists only as an inert placeholder (§5).
- **Failure contract** — The `{ code, message, retryable }` shape returned by every backend error (13 closed codes; see §Cross-Cutting NFRs), consumed by every repository as `Either<Failure, T>`.

## Information Architecture

- **Entrance/auth surfaces:** Splash (auto-advance) → Biometric Vault (Face ID/Touch ID, PIN fallback) → Login/Signup (single screen, toggled).
- **Home/Chat** is the base authenticated surface, with three overlays that can appear on top of it without navigating away: the Sessão Expirada overlay (FR-2), an offline banner (FR-27), and the Insertion Modal (§4.3). The side menu (☰), opened from here, leads to Chat Session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, and Planos de Ação `[ext]`.
- **Meus Registros (timeline)** carries its own overlay: the Export sheet (§4.10), plus an inline filter sheet and search bar (§4.6).
- **Configurações** hosts the dashboard (§4.11), inline profile editing, and the account-deletion confirmation dialog (§8 OQ-4).

## 4. Features

*Where an FR's testable condition is a single, self-evident clause, it is folded into the FR's statement itself rather than broken out into a separate Consequences block; the separate block is used once an FR needs more than one distinct, checkable condition.*

### 4.1 Foundation & Session Management

**Description:** The scaffold every other feature depends on: an authenticated-session lifecycle, the app shell and base navigation, and the one cross-cutting overlay — the Sessão Expirada overlay — that can interrupt any screen. Delivered first (F000) because every unit after it assumes these exist. Realizes UJ-1, UJ-2 (edge case).

#### FR-1: Account creation and authentication

A user can create an account and log in with email/password, and the app can silently refresh or verify the session without forcing a re-login on every app open.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Signup, login, refresh, and session-check each round-trip through their respective backend operations and surface the Failure contract on error.
- A valid, unexpired session persists across app restarts without re-prompting for credentials.
- `[ASSUMPTION]` Signup collects email + password only, matching the single-screen toggle shown in the prototype (no password-confirmation or display-name field) — see §8 OQ-2.

#### FR-2: Expired-session recovery overlay

When the backend reports an expired session, the app shows a "Sessão expirada" overlay on top of the current screen rather than navigating away from it.

**Consequences (testable):**
- The screen underneath (including scroll position and in-progress state, e.g. an open chat) is preserved while the overlay is shown.
- "Entrar novamente" routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow (RF03), not a full logout-and-login form.
- The overlay can appear while viewing the timeline (RF07, called out explicitly in requirements.md as session-dependent) or chat (RF04, shown as the "Sessão expirada" state in `prototype-extract.md`).

#### FR-3: Base navigation shell

The app provides navigation between Home/Chat, the side menu, Meus Registros, and Configurações, with clearly marked placeholders for RF01–RF10 functionality not yet built in this unit.

**Consequences (testable):**
- All four surfaces are reachable from app launch without requiring any RF01–RF10 feature to be implemented.
- Placeholders are visually distinguishable from finished screens (no silent dead ends that look complete).

### 4.2 Biometric Authentication Vault (RF03)

**Description:** A device-validated access barrier in front of all user data. Realizes UJ-1 (entry + edge case).

#### FR-4: App-access gate

The app requires Face ID, Touch ID, or PIN before showing any user data, on cold start and after the idle timeout (FR-6).

**Consequences (testable):**
- No screen other than the vault/login screen is reachable before authentication succeeds.
- No biometric data or biometric call ever reaches the backend — validation is 100% on-device.

#### FR-5: Biometric-failure fallback to PIN

A failed biometric attempt offers PIN entry as an alternative and never locks the user out of their own app.

**Consequences (testable):**
- After a biometric failure, a PIN entry path is always reachable (Tela 0.1c).
- Repeated biometric failures that trigger an OS-level lockout are detected and routed to the app's own PIN fallback rather than retried against the OS.

#### FR-6: Fixed idle re-authentication timeout

Returning to the app from the background after 5 minutes requires re-authentication; this value is fixed, not user-configurable.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Resuming before 5 minutes elapsed does not prompt re-authentication.
- Resuming after 5 minutes always prompts re-authentication, regardless of any user setting.

#### FR-7: Biometric preference persistence

The user's choice to enable/disable biometric gating is saved server-side via `PATCH /account/settings` and survives both app restarts and reinstalls, since the value is fetched from the account, not cached only on-device.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Disabling biometrics still leaves PIN as the access method — the vault itself cannot be turned off entirely.

### 4.3 Multimodal Capture (RF01)

**Description:** The single entry point for creating a journal Entry, in text, audio, or photo form, all through the Insertion Modal. Realizes UJ-1.

#### FR-8: Text Entry capture

A user can type free text in the Insertion Modal and save it as an Entry (source=`manual`).

#### FR-9: Audio Entry capture

A user can record audio in the Insertion Modal; the raw recording becomes the basis of an Entry (source=`audio`) once processed (RF02).

#### FR-10: Photo Entry capture

A user can capture or select a photo in the Insertion Modal; it becomes the basis of an Entry (source=`photo`) once processed (RF02).

**Consequences (testable, FR-8 through FR-10):**
- All three modalities produce the same persisted Entry shape — none is structurally special-cased after capture.
- Each call to `POST /entries` carries the correct `source` value for its modality.

#### FR-11: Cancel-safe capture

Interrupting a capture in progress (e.g., stopping a recording before saving, backing out mid-photo) never creates a partial or empty Entry.

**Consequences (testable):**
- No `POST /entries` call fires for an abandoned capture.
- `[OPEN]` Switching tabs mid-recording (e.g. Áudio → Foto) is undefined behavior in the current prototype — see §8 OQ-3.

### 4.4 Speech-to-Text / OCR Processing (RF02)

**Description:** Turns raw audio into text on-device, and raw photos into text via the backend, before an Entry is persisted. Realizes UJ-1.

#### FR-12: On-device audio transcription

Recorded audio is transcribed to text entirely on-device via `whisper_ggml`; the audio file itself is never sent to the backend.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Exactly four visible states occur in sequence or on failure: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry, media never discarded.
- No network call containing audio bytes is made at any point in this pipeline.

#### FR-13: Backend OCR for photos

A captured photo is sent to `POST /media/ocr` to extract text before the Entry is created.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Mirrors FR-12's four-state pattern: capture → processing OCR → recognized → (on failure) error with retry, photo never discarded.
- On OCR failure, the user has two recovery paths, not one: retry the OCR step, or save the Entry with no extracted text ("Salvar só a foto") — both are shown in the prototype's OCR-failure state.
- `OCR_NO_TEXT` (no extractable text found) is handled as a distinct, user-visible outcome, not a generic failure.

**Notes:** Test material for both pipelines — sample audio, OCR test images, and expected transcription output — lives in `docs/input/backend/fixtures/`.
