### 4.5 Multi-Source History / Timeline (RF07)

**Description:** A chronological view of every Entry regardless of origin, each carrying a Sync Badge. Realizes UJ-1 (as the destination for captured entries) and UJ-4 (as the surface search/filter operates on).

#### FR-14: Chronological Entry list

All Entries, from any source, are listed together grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.

#### FR-15: Per-entry Sync Badge

Each Entry shows one of three Sync Badge states, derived client-side from `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` and local pending-write state — the backend exposes no `sync_status` field.

**Consequences (testable):**
- A freshly created Entry shows "Synchronizing" until the server's write confirmation is reconciled, then "Synchronized."
- A write that fails (network or any Failure-contract code) shows "Synchronization error" until a subsequent successful write reconciles it.
- The badge's update stream runs independently of the auth/session stream — a pending sync-badge transition is never blocked, delayed, or cleared by session-expiry handling (FR-17).
- `[OPEN]` No retry affordance is visible on the error state in the current prototype — see §8 OQ-6.

#### FR-16: Empty-state handling

With zero Entries, the screen shows a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture, not a blank list.

#### FR-17: Session-expiry resilience mid-view

If the session expires while viewing the timeline, the FR-2 overlay appears without crashing or losing scroll position.

#### FR-18: Entry detail view

A user can open a single Entry from the timeline to see its full content, via `GET /entries/:id`.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Opening an Entry never mutates it — there is no edit affordance, consistent with Entries being immutable (§3 Glossary).
- A detail request for an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user returns `NOT_FOUND` (RNF04), not a permission-denied code.

**Feature-specific NFRs:** No BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly — the three streams this screen composes (auth status, Sync Badge state, and Entry data) combine only through the domain layer, never via a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.

### 4.6 Semantic Search / Filter (RF06)

**Description:** Meaning-based search plus metadata filters over the timeline from §4.5. Realizes UJ-4.

#### FR-19: Semantic search

A user can search Entries by meaning, not just literal keyword match (e.g. "ansiedade" matches an entry that only used "nervosismo"), via `GET /entries/search`.

#### FR-20: Metadata filters

A user can filter by source and date range (`dateFrom`/`dateTo`); no tag/category filter exists, since categorization is an extension feature (§5). Filtering with no active search term queries `GET /entries`; filtering combined with an active search term queries `GET /entries/search`, carrying the same filter parameters.

**Consequences (testable, FR-19/FR-20):**
- Multiple active filters combine with AND semantics.
- `[OPEN]` How an active text search and active filters interact when both are set simultaneously is unspecified in the prototype — see §8 OQ-7.

#### FR-21: Debounced search input

Search input is debounced by 300ms before firing a request.

#### FR-22: Non-disruptive filter clearing

Clearing active filters restores the full list in place, without a full screen reload, and the cache stays duplicate-free after a reconnect (cloud-only; offline is view-only for this screen).

**Notes:** Test material (a seeded set of entries with known semantic relationships, for verifying true meaning-based matches) lives in `docs/input/backend/fixtures/seeded-search-entries.md`.

### 4.7 Interactive Chat with Memory / RAG (RF04)

**Description:** The core differentiator (§1): a persistent, multi-session conversation where the assistant answers using RAG over the user's own Entries. Realizes UJ-2.

#### FR-23: Send message, receive RAG-grounded streaming response

A user sends a Chat Message and receives a streamed response grounded in semantic retrieval over their own Entries, via SSE on `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Exactly three visible states exist: streaming/processing, error, complete.
- Chat Messages never automatically create Entries — RF10 is the sole, explicit exception.

#### FR-24: Multi-session chat history

A user can hold multiple named Chat Sessions, listed and switchable from the side menu.

#### FR-25: New-conversation action

A user can start a new Chat Session from the side menu.

**Consequences (testable):**
- `POST /chat/sessions` is blocked offline — starting a new Chat Session requires connectivity, consistent with the offline composer lock on existing conversations (FR-27).

#### FR-26: Dropped-stream resilience

If a response stream drops mid-generation, the partial message stays on screen with a failure indicator; the user can retry via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry`, which regenerates without duplicating the original question.

#### FR-27: Offline composer lock

When offline, the message composer is disabled while the existing conversation history remains visible and navigable.

### 4.8 Save Chat Message as Entry (RF10)

**Description:** Lets a user turn their own Chat Message into a real Entry. Realizes UJ-3. Depends on RF01 and RF04.

#### FR-28: Bookmark a user message into an Entry

A "save" affordance appears only on the user's own Chat Messages (never on AI responses) and, when used, creates an Entry (source=`chat`, carrying `chatMessageId`) through the same shared entries use case RF01 defines — never by importing the entries repository or data source directly (RNF06).

#### FR-29: Idempotent save

Saving the same Chat Message more than once does not create a duplicate Entry and never surfaces a conflict error (the backend returns 200, not 409).

#### FR-30: Save-failure isolation

If the save fails, the surrounding Chat Session remains fully usable, and the save affordance resets to a retryable state rather than freezing.

### 4.9 Proactive Insights (RF08)

**Description:** The mechanism by which the assistant injects an unprompted suggestion into the conversation. Scope is the trigger/injection mechanism only — the quality of the generated Insight text is explicitly out of scope for acceptance testing. Realizes UJ-2 (the unprompted-Insight moment within an ongoing conversation). Depends on RF04.

#### FR-31: Unprompted Insight injection

An Insight is injected into the active Chat Session once per satisfied condition — triggered by either 5 user messages sent or 2 minutes of inactivity, whichever occurs first — via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight`.

#### FR-32: Insight failure isolation

A failure to generate an Insight does not interrupt or break the main chat experience.

**Consequences (testable):**
- The message composer remains enabled and no error overlay appears over the conversation when Insight generation fails.
- The user can keep sending and receiving ordinary Chat Messages (FR-23) uninterrupted; only the Insight itself is absent.

#### FR-33: Non-disruptive dismissal

Dismissing an Insight does not affect scroll position or any other conversation state.

### 4.10 Personal Summary Export (RF05)

**Description:** On-demand generation of a narrative PDF summary plus an always-available raw-data download. Scope is job/file/failure handling only — the quality of the generated narrative text is explicitly out of scope for acceptance testing. Realizes UJ-5. Depends on RF07.

#### FR-34: Request a period export

A user can request an export for a chosen date period via `POST /export/summary`.

#### FR-35: Job status across five screen states

The export sheet reflects the job's progress across five states — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio — via `GET /export/:jobId/status`, which reports `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) independently.

#### FR-36: Narrative-independent raw-data download

Raw data is downloadable via `GET /export/:jobId/download` as soon as it's ready, even if the AI narrative step is still processing, has failed, or was skipped — the narrative never blocks the data download.

#### FR-37: Empty-period handling

Requesting an export for a period with zero Entries surfaces "Período vazio" with no download offered and no crash.

### 4.11 Temporal Summaries / Dashboard & Account (RF09)

**Description:** The Configurações screen's evolution Dashboard, plus the profile and account actions that live there. Scope for the Dashboard is aggregation/rendering only — AI narrative text quality is explicitly out of scope for acceptance testing. Realizes UJ-6. Depends on F000, RF01.

#### FR-38: On-demand dashboard aggregation

Opening Configurações computes and renders an evolution chart via `GET /dashboard/aggregate`, correctly at zero, one, and more-than-thirty Entries.

#### FR-39: Independent narrative text

A separate narrative text is fetched via `GET /dashboard/narrative`; its failure is a distinct, chart-still-renders state, never blocking the chart (two independent endpoints by design).

#### FR-40: Cache invalidation on new Entry

The dashboard's aggregation recalculates after a new Entry is created elsewhere in the app; since Entries are immutable, invalidation only ever needs to trigger on create, never on edit.

#### FR-41: Profile name editing

A user can edit their display name inline on Configurações via `PATCH /account/settings`.

#### FR-42: Logout

"Sair" ends the session (`POST /auth/logout`) and returns to the Biometric Vault / login screen.

#### FR-43: Account deletion

"Apagar conta" shows a confirmation dialog; on confirmation, the account and all associated data are hard-deleted (`DELETE /account`, LGPD-driven), and the user is routed to the same destination as logout.

**Notes:** `[NOTE FOR PM]` No dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists in the current prototype (§8 OQ-4) — revisit if post-defense polish time exists.

## 5. Non-Goals (Explicit)

- **Dynamic AI categorization of Entries** `[ext]` — downgraded to manual, user-created tags on Meus Registros; no AI logic behind it.
- **Autonomous AI goal extraction** `[ext]` — exists only as a static Action Plans Kanban screen with no underlying logic.
- **Dynamic AI persona adjustment** `[ext]` — exists only as a cosmetic Settings selector (Analítico/Empático/Socrático) that does not change assistant behavior in this delivery.
- **Any risk-signal detection** (self-harm, suicidal ideation) — a deliberate scope exclusion tied to the product's non-clinical stance (§1), not an oversight. A low-cost static crisis-resources disclaimer is a candidate fast-follow, not committed (§8 OQ-8).
- **Entry editing or deletion** — no such backend operation exists; Entries are permanent once created.
- **Offline Entry creation** — all writes are cloud-only; offline mode is view-only for already-synced data.
- **Android, or any platform beyond iOS portrait** for this delivery.
- **Any change to the backend, its contract, or its configuration** — consumed exactly as documented.
- **Any direct call to an AI provider (Claude, Voyage AI) from the app** — every AI-touching operation goes through the backend.
- **Grading or verifying the quality of AI-generated text** (Insights, export narratives, dashboard narrative) — RF05/RF08/RF09 are scoped to mechanism, failure-handling, and UI-safety only; generated-content quality is explicitly out of acceptance scope per requirements.md. (RF04's chat responses and RF06's search-result relevance carry no such explicit exclusion in requirements.md — see §8 OQ-10.)

## 7. Success Metrics

*This is an academic capstone with no customer-acquisition or adoption target; success is defined by specification conformance, not usage.* Stated plainly: this PRD's graded metrics (SM-1–3) can only confirm the RAG-memory mechanism is wired correctly end-to-end — whether the memory bet (§1) actually pays off for a real user is not a graded surface for this delivery (SM-5 is deliberately informal and uninstrumented; see also §8 OQ-10).

**Primary**
- **SM-1**: Every acceptance criterion stated per-RF in requirements.md §1 passes. Validates FR-1 through FR-43, the feature-specific NFRs called out in §4 (e.g. the BLoC-composition rule under §4.5 FR-18), and RNF01's performance thresholds (manual timing spot-check per module, not automated).
- **SM-2**: Zero Clean Architecture layer violations (RNF06) and ≥80% domain-layer test coverage (RNF07), verified across all 11 feature modules.
- **SM-3**: All 15 required network-failure scenarios (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types) are handled per the Failure contract, with zero unhandled exceptions (RNF09).

**Secondary**
- **SM-4**: Zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart` (RNF08), verified by inspection.
- **SM-5** *(qualitative, informal)*: the assistant surfaces something true from weeks earlier without being asked to, and the act of writing starts to feel worth repeating. No instrumentation planned to measure this for v1 — it is a design intent, not a graded criterion.

**Counter-metrics (do not optimize)**
- **SM-C1**: Scope creep into AI-generated content *quality* work (better prompts, better narratives) — explicitly out of grading scope (§5) and would divert effort from the mechanism work that is actually graded. Counterbalances SM-1.
- **SM-C2**: Test coverage inflated with trivial/tautological tests to hit the RNF07 80% number — the metric is domain-layer correctness, not a percentage. Counterbalances SM-2.

## 8. Open Questions

1. **No project timeline, deadline, or defense date is stated anywhere in the source documents.** This blocks any confident sequencing/pacing judgment for downstream epics work. *(Flagged by the PRFAQ distillate as the single biggest open input.)*
2. **Signup field set is underspecified.** The prototype shows one screen toggled between Entrar/Criar conta with only email+password fields visible — no password confirmation, no display-name capture at signup. Confirm this is intentional before building FR-1. *(blocks F000 — build unit 1 of 11)*
3. **Tab-switching mid-capture in the Insertion Modal is undefined** (e.g., switching from Áudio to Foto while a recording is in progress) — decide: discard, warn, or persist the in-progress capture (affects FR-11). *(blocks RF01 — build unit 3 of 11)*
4. **No "account deleted" or "signed out" confirmation screen exists** — both flows dead-end at the Biometric Vault screen. Decide whether this is acceptable for v1 or needs even a lightweight confirmation (affects FR-42/FR-43). *(blocks RF09 — build unit 11 of 11; lowest urgency of the sequenced OQs)*
5. **(Already resolved, kept here only for visibility — not a live open question.)** Cloud-only, immutable-entry design is a backend constraint, not a product choice: there is no appetite to request a contract change (confirmed — none per `AGENTS.md`); recorded so it isn't silently re-discovered as a "bug" later.
6. **The Sync Badge error state has no visible retry affordance in the current prototype** — decide whether the badge needs one, or whether reconciliation on the next successful write is sufficient (affects FR-15). *(blocks RF07 — build unit 5 of 11)*
7. **Combined search + filter behavior is unspecified** — when both a search term and active filters are set, decide the intended interaction (AND-combine vs. one overriding the other) (affects FR-19/FR-20). *(blocks RF06 — build unit 6 of 11)*
8. **A static, no-logic crisis-resources disclaimer was recommended (PRFAQ) as a low-cost way to close the "silent gap" left by having no risk-signal detection**, without contradicting the non-clinical stance (§1, §5). Not yet decided for inclusion.
9. **Whether Cerne continues as a maintained portfolio piece after the defense, or ends as a one-time academic artifact**, is unresolved and would change how much polish-time investment in OQ-2/OQ-4/OQ-6/OQ-7 is worth it.
10. **Whether RF04's chat-response quality, and separately RF06's search-result quality, should carry the same "mechanism only, never graded" boundary that requirements.md states explicitly for RF05/RF08/RF09 is unstated for both.** Treated here as a genuine gap for each, not silently extended or silently dropped (§5, §Constraints and Guardrails). *(blocks grading boundary for RF04 — build unit 7 of 11 — and RF06 — build unit 6 of 11)*
11. **"Cerne" is a working title** — confirm or replace.

## 9. Assumptions Index

- §2.1/§2.3 — The target-user persona (functional/emotional/social JTBD, the "Mara" journeys) is reconstructed from the product brief and PRFAQ, not stated verbatim in `docs/input/`.
- §4.1 FR-1 — Signup is assumed to collect only email + password (see OQ-2 for the decision this depends on).

## Cross-Cutting NFRs

- **RNF01 (performance):** Local UI interactions respond in <100ms; any network call taking >300ms shows a loading indicator. Verified via manual timing spot-checks during each feature module's QA pass (SM-1) — no automated performance instrumentation is planned for this delivery.
- **RNF02 (PII handling)** `[inherited, not verified by this delivery]`: PII stripping runs via a Claude Haiku 4.5 structured prompt/tool-use step (not a dedicated NER model), server-side only.
- **RNF03 (data retention)** `[inherited, not verified by this delivery]`: Zero data retention by upstream AI providers.
- **RNF04 (data isolation):** Row Level Security (Supabase) enforces per-user data isolation; the client never needs its own authorization logic for cross-user access — the backend uniformly returns `NOT_FOUND` (never a permission-denied code) for any resource that doesn't belong to the requesting user, so existence of other users' data is never revealed.
- **RNF05 (account deletion):** Hard delete of account and all associated data on request (LGPD).
- **RNF06 (architecture):** Zero Clean Architecture layer violations — the domain layer imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything from a `data/` layer, in any of the 11 feature modules.
- **RNF07 (test coverage):** ≥80% domain-layer test coverage.
- **RNF08 (visual fidelity):** Visual fidelity to the prototype (color, typography, spacing); zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`.
- **RNF09 (resilience):** Every repository returns `Either<Failure, T>`; 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types (timeout, malformed response, no connection) = 15 tested failure scenarios, zero unhandled exceptions.

**The Failure contract** — every backend error has the shape `{ code, message, retryable }`, drawn from a closed set of 13 codes (the one extra client-only case, a malformed/unparseable response, is handled identically but never retryable):

| Code | Retryable | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| AUTH_EXPIRED | no | access token expired — triggers the FR-2 overlay |
| AUTH_INVALID | no | invalid credentials (password login only — never originates from biometrics, since biometric validation is on-device) |
| NETWORK_TIMEOUT | yes | request timed out |
| NETWORK_OFFLINE | yes | connection ended with no HTTP response at all — must be handled as a distinct "no response received" branch, not dispatched on a status code |
| VALIDATION_ERROR | no | malformed request payload |
| PII_CHECK_FAILED | yes | server-side PII scan step failed |
| EMBEDDING_FAILED | yes | embedding generation failed |
| AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT | yes | AI generation step timed out |
| NOT_FOUND | no | resource missing, or belongs to another user (RNF04) |
| RATE_LIMITED | yes | too many requests |
| EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD | no | export requested for a period with no Entries (FR-37) |
| PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE | no | upload exceeds size limit |
| OCR_NO_TEXT | no | OCR found no extractable text (FR-13) |

## Constraints and Guardrails

Privacy, safety, and platform constraints are stated once each, at the FR/NFR/Non-Goal that owns them, rather than restated here. Index:

- **Privacy** — on-device-only audio and biometrics (FR-12, FR-4), zero AI-provider data retention (RNF03), server-side PII stripping (RNF02), RLS-enforced data isolation (RNF04).
- **Safety** — non-clinical framing and no risk-signal detection (§1, §5), the mechanism-only AI-content-quality boundary and its two open exceptions, RF04 and RF06 (§5, §8 OQ-10).
- **Platform** — iOS portrait-only, frozen backend contract, no direct AI-provider calls from the app (§5).

## Aesthetic and Tone

The prototype (`docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §3) defines a named visual token system — color, typography, spacing, radii, elevation, and iconography — that `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` must be the single source of truth for; no visual value may appear hardcoded anywhere else in the app (RNF08). Interface copy throughout the product is in Brazilian Portuguese. Tone follows directly from §1's stance: reflective and private, never clinical, never styled as a "companion" the user is meant to bond with.

---
*Addendum: `addendum.md` in this folder holds implementation-level decisions (routing, HTTP client, local cache, DI, package choices and rejected alternatives), competitive-landscape and market-sizing detail, regulatory citations, and corrections-carried-forward from prior planning sessions — none of it duplicated here.*

23	
24	# Architecture Spine — Cerne
25	
26	## Design Paradigm
27	
28	**Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature, BLoC on top, errors carried as values.**
29	
30	- `presentation/` (BLoC/Cubit + widgets) → depends on → `domain/` (entities, use cases, repository/port interfaces) ← implemented by ← `data/` (DTOs, data sources, repository implementations).
31	- `domain/` is the only layer every other layer may depend on; it depends on nothing feature-specific and never on `package:flutter` (RNF06).
32	- Every operation that can fail (network, parse, local I/O) returns `Either<Failure, T>` (`fpdart`) at the repository boundary — no repository throws past itself (RNF09).
33	- `core/` sits beneath every feature and holds the only cross-feature-shared code: the `Failure` hierarchy, the API client/URL builder, the DI bootstrap, the local-cache boxes, `Resource<T>`, `isolatedSideEffect`, design tokens, and the `SessionStatus` contract.
34	
35	```mermaid
36	flowchart TD
37	    subgraph Feature["any lib/features/<name>/"]
38	        P["presentation (BLoC/Cubit, widgets)"]
39	        D["domain (entities, use cases, port interfaces)"]
40	        DA["data (DTOs, data sources, repository impl)"]
41	        P --> D
42	        DA --> D
43	    end
44	    Core["core/ (Failure, ApiClient, DI, cache, Resource<T>, SessionStatus, VaultStatus, design_tokens)"]
45	    D --> Core
46	    DA --> Core
47	    OtherDomain["another feature's domain/ (port interfaces only)"]
48	    P -.->|"AD-6: cross-feature calls only through the owning feature's domain port"| OtherDomain
49	```
50	
51	## Invariants & Rules
52	
53	### AD-1 — Layer dependency direction (RNF06)
54	
55	- **Binds:** all features
56	- **Prevents:** `domain/` depending on Flutter, on any `data/` (own or another feature's), or on another feature's `presentation/`.
57	- **Rule:** dependency direction is strictly `presentation → domain ← data`. `domain/` imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything under any `data/`. Only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins. `presentation/` never imports a feature's own or another feature's `data/` directly.
58	
59	### AD-2 — Either-everywhere error channel (RNF09)
60	
61	- **Binds:** all repositories (read and write)
62	- **Prevents:** a feature inventing its own error signaling (exceptions crossing the repository boundary, nullable returns, ad hoc string errors) that other code can't pattern-match generically.
63	- **Rule:** every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream). `Failure` is the closed hierarchy in AD-3. No repository implementation lets a native/dio exception escape unmapped.
64	
65	### AD-3 — Closed `Failure` hierarchy `[ADOPTED]`
66	
67	- **Binds:** all
68	- **Prevents:** two features inventing different shapes for "network timeout," or silently dropping one of the server's 13 codes.
69	- **Rule:** one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes — the 13 from `error-taxonomy.md` (`AuthExpired`, `AuthInvalid`, `NetworkTimeout`, `NetworkOffline`, `Validation`, `PiiCheckFailed`, `EmbeddingFailed`, `AiGenerationTimeout`, `NotFound`, `RateLimited`, `ExportEmptyPeriod`, `PayloadTooLarge`, `OcrNoText`) plus the local-only `MalformedResponse` (`retryable` hardcoded `false`, for the client's own parse-failure detection). Never redefined or subset per feature. `AuthInvalid` can only ever originate from `POST /auth/login` — no biometric/PIN check ever reaches the server (AD-14), so no feature maps a local vault failure to this code.
70	
71	### AD-4 — Retry policy lives in exactly one place `[ADOPTED]`
72	
73	- **Binds:** the API client
74	- **Prevents:** a feature writing its own retry loop that double-retries, or retries a `retryable:false` code.
75	- **Rule:** retry logic is implemented once (the `dio` interceptor / `ApiClient` wrapper), fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes (`NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_OFFLINE`, `PII_CHECK_FAILED`, `EMBEDDING_FAILED`, `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMITED`). Every other code surfaces once, unretried.
76	
77	### AD-5 — Function-name URL construction and header policy
78	
79	- **Binds:** every network call
80	- **Prevents:** a feature string-concatenating the literal `openapi.yaml` REST path (which is not a real URL) or re-deciding which `Authorization` value to send.
81	- **Rule:** one URL builder in `core/` maps each operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>`. One `dio` interceptor owns headers: `apikey` on every call; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` only on the three `security: []` operations (signup, login, refresh); `Authorization: Bearer <user token>` on every other (`bearerAuth`) operation.
82	
83	### AD-6 — `entries` owns `Entry` from RF01 onward; every other feature reaches it only through a domain-layer port
84	
85	- **Binds:** RF01 (capture → entries, the *first* consumer — delivery order builds RF01 three units before RF06/RF07), RF10 (chat → entries), and any future cross-feature dependency
86	- **Prevents:** (a) RF01 inventing its own local `Entry` model/repository/cache box because `features/entries/` "doesn't exist yet" at its position in the delivery order, which RF06/RF07 would then duplicate; (b) any feature reaching into `entries`'s `data/`, repository, data source, or BLoC — the exact violation RF10's acceptance criteria calls out, which would also break RNF06.
87	- **Rule:** `features/entries/` is scaffolded at RF01 (not RF06/RF07) because RF01 is the first unit that must call `POST /entries` (requirements.md §6.2). From RF01 on, `entries/domain` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create`, `read` — see AD-11), and the entries Hive box. `entries` exposes an abstract `CreateEntryUseCase`/`SaveEntryUseCase`-shaped port; RF01's `capture` feature and RF10's `chat` feature are both *consumers* — each only ever imports and injects that abstract type from `entries/domain`, never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`. RF06/RF07 extend the same `EntriesRepository` port with `list`/`search` methods; they do not introduce a second entry model or a second owner. The port's `create` is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`: a second call for a `chatMessageId` that already has an entry never creates a duplicate — the implementation (not the port's type signature) is responsible for this check, binding on RF10's build.
88	
89	### AD-7 — No BLoC-to-BLoC references
90	
91	- **Binds:** all (generalizes RF07's explicit AC to every feature)
92	- **Prevents:** hidden coupling and circular-rebuild chains between presentation units built independently.
93	- **Rule:** a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency, same-feature or cross-feature. Composition of multiple independent state sources happens by injecting the underlying `domain/` streams/use-cases into each BLoC independently, or via `BlocListener`/`MultiBlocListener` in the widget tree — never a direct BLoC → BLoC reference.
94	
95	### AD-8 — Single `SessionStatus` source of truth
96	
97	- **Binds:** F000 (go_router redirect), RF07 (composite auth × sync × data state), any feature that needs session validity
98	- **Prevents:** two independently-built screens disagreeing on what "session expired" means or when to prompt re-login.
99	- **Rule:** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream, exposed from the auth feature's `domain/`, registered once in DI as a singleton. Every consumer injects/listens to that stream; none re-derives session state from a raw 401, from its own `GET /auth/session` poll, or from a second stream. `SessionStatus` governs *server session validity only* — it composes with the local vault gate per AD-14, it does not replace it.
100	
101	### AD-9 — Cloud-only: no offline write queue
102	
103	- **Binds:** all repositories (generalizes RF06's "cloud-only" note and RF04's "blocked offline" writes)
104	- **Prevents:** a feature building a local write-queue/outbox that silently diverges from "offline permits viewing cached data only."
105	- **Rule:** a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)` — it is never queued for later. Plain reads (`GET /entries`, `GET /chat/sessions`, `GET .../messages`) transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache. **Semantic search is the one read exception:** `GET /entries/search` has no client-side vector index to fall back to, so with no connectivity it also resolves to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)`, same as a write — it is never served from cache. The only client-side "pending write" state is transient, in-memory, scoped to one in-flight request (it feeds AD-10's `Synchronizing` badge state) — it is never persisted as a queue.
106	
107	### AD-10 — Sync badge is a pure client-side derivation (locks `sync-badge.md`)
108	
109	- **Binds:** every screen that renders the per-entry sync badge (chat save confirmation, My Records list, any future one)
110	- **Prevents:** two screens computing `Synchronizing`/`Error`/`Synchronized` differently.
111	- **Rule:** one derivation function lives in `entries/domain`, computed from three inputs: `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and the transient per-entry write state (AD-9) — which is itself one of three values: no pending write (→ `Synchronized`), a write in flight (→ `Synchronizing`), or the in-flight write's `Future` resolved to `Left(Failure)` (→ `Synchronization error`, held until the next write attempt reconciles it). Every screen consumes that function's output; none recomputes the badge inline. The server never supplies a `sync_status` field — `requirements.md` §8 is wrong on this point (`sync-badge.md` and the `Entry` schema win).
112	
113	### AD-11 — Entry immutability
114	
115	- **Binds:** the entries feature
116	- **Prevents:** a unit speculatively adding an update/delete path the backend doesn't support.
117	- **Rule:** `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read operations only. No update or delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`.
118	
119	### AD-12 — Shared view-state scoped to single-source-of-truth fetches `[ADOPTED]`
120	
121	- **Binds:** RF06 (search results), RF09 (dashboard aggregate/narrative) — explicitly *not* RF02, RF04, or RF07
122	- **Prevents:** forcing a composite or multi-stage state machine into a generic fetch enum, and the reverse: ad hoc one-off state shapes where a shared one would do.
123	- **Rule:** generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) lives in `core/`, used only by screens with one data source and one fetch lifecycle. RF02's capture pipeline (`recording`/`processing`/`transcribed`/`error`), RF07's composite auth × sync × data state, and RF04's chat message stream (append-only, streaming/SSE, not a single fetch) each define their own sealed state class — never forced into `Resource<T>`. RF08's proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto RF04's existing chat state, not a parallel `Resource<T>`.
124	
125	### AD-13 — `isolatedSideEffect` contract fixed now, implementation deferred `[ADOPTED]`
126	
127	- **Binds:** RF08, RF10 (both state the identical failure-isolation requirement)
128	- **Prevents:** RF08 reinventing its own failure-isolation wrapper (or importing RF10's feature-local one), producing two incompatible "never block the caller on failure" implementations.
129	- **Rule:** `core/` holds a never-throws helper with signature `Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped (never throws past itself); it ships with RF10, delivery order's first consumer (RF04 → RF10 → RF08), not built speculatively in F000. The helper's own `Future` always completes independently of the caller: RF10 may `await` it before updating its button state, and RF08 must be able to call it **without** awaiting (fire-and-forget) so a slow/failed insight generation never blocks or delays the chat stream. RF08 reuses it from `core/` without a cross-feature import.
130	
131	### AD-14 — One `go_router` redirect composes exactly two gates, in a fixed order: vault, then session
132	
133	- **Binds:** F000 (builds the redirect skeleton + `SessionStatus` half), RF03 (plugs the vault half into the same redirect)
134	- **Prevents:** F000 and RF03 each building an independent navigation gate (two competing `redirect` callbacks, or RF03 bolting a second check onto screens individually) — `go_router` supports only one top-level `redirect`, so two independently-built gates cannot both "just work."
135	- **Rule:** the redirect composes exactly two domain-level streams, evaluated in this order: (1) `VaultStatus` (local-only — biometric/PIN unlocked, Face-ID-failed-offer-PIN, or locked after the 5-minute background timeout; RF03 exposes it from `features/vault/domain` the same way auth exposes `SessionStatus`, AD-8) — checked *first*, before any network state, because it gates whether the app may show anything at all; then (2) `SessionStatus` (AD-8) once the vault is unlocked. Neither gate ever reaches the server to validate itself (`POST /auth/login` is the only path that can produce `AuthInvalid`, per AD-3) — the vault is validated entirely on-device, consistent with the backend having no biometric-unlock endpoint.
136	
137	### AD-15 — The local cache is a projection, never a query engine
138	
139	- **Binds:** `entries`, `chat` — every feature with a `hive_ce` box `[ADOPTED, promoted from the F000 forge session]`
140	- **Prevents:** a unit adding local filtering, joining, or sorting logic "for performance" or "for offline support," which would then disagree with the server's own filter semantics (AD-9's offline read rule assumes the cache's content is a verbatim copy, not a re-derived view).
141	- **Rule:** every query dimension (`source`, `dateFrom`/`dateTo`, semantic search, pagination cursor) is a server-side query parameter per `openapi.yaml`. A `hive_ce` box stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id (or by session id for messages); no feature ever filters, joins, sorts, or re-derives a different view from a cached collection — a cache miss or a dimension not covered by AD-9's offline-read rule surfaces `Failure.networkOffline`, it is never approximated locally.
142	
143	## Consistency Conventions
144	
145	| Concern | Convention |
146	| --- | --- |
147	| Feature naming | `lib/features/<feature>/` one of: `auth`, `vault`, `capture`, `entries`, `chat`, `export`, `dashboard`, `account` — see Capability → Architecture Map |
148	| Errors | `Failure` sealed hierarchy (AD-3) everywhere; UI maps a `Failure` to copy using its `retryable` flag, never a hardcoded per-screen message list |
149	| IDs & dates | server-assigned string IDs and ISO-8601 timestamps passed through verbatim from DTOs (`freezed`+`json_serializable`); the client never generates or reformats an entity ID |
150	| Visual values | `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` only (RNF08) — no color/font/spacing/radius literal anywhere else |
151	| Network envelope | one `ApiClient`/URL-builder + one header interceptor (AD-5); no feature constructs a request URL or header set itself |
152	| State composition | `Resource<T>` for single-source fetches (AD-12); no BLoC-to-BLoC references (AD-7) |
153	| Testing | `mocktail` stubs one `ApiClient` interface per repository test, not a fake transport layer; one shared table-driven helper drives the 5-write-endpoints × 3-failure-types = 15-scenario matrix (RNF09); ≥80% line coverage gate on every `domain/` (RNF07) |
154	| Config/secrets | `.env` (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) loaded via `flutter_dotenv` `[ASSUMPTION — settled here; requirements.md left it "free," no prior session decided it]`; never committed, never hardcoded |
155	| AI provider access | the app never calls Claude or Voyage AI directly — every AI-backed feature goes through the backend's documented endpoints (project policy, binding on all features) |
156	| Local cache | `hive_ce` boxes are a projection of server responses, never a query engine (AD-15) |
157	| Pagination/cursor | every paginated list (`entries`, `entries/search`, `chat_sessions`, `chat_messages`) uses the server's own cursor convention verbatim; the cursor string is cached alongside the box it pages (AD-15) — `entries` and `entries/search` share one cursor convention since both live in the one `entries` feature (AD-6) |
158	| Fixed numeric parameters (`requirements.md` §10 — not reinterpretable) | background session timeout 5 min (RF03) · search debounce 300 ms (RF06) · proactive-insight trigger N=5 user messages OR T=2 min inactivity, fires once per satisfied condition (RF08) · dashboard rendering scenarios 0 / 1 / >30 entries (RF09) · local UI latency <100 ms, loading indicator threshold >300 ms (RNF01) · domain coverage ≥80% (RNF07) · 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types = 15 scenarios (RNF09) — each is implemented inside its owning feature (not a shared core constant), but none may be approximated or re-tuned by whichever unit builds it |
159	
160	## Stack
161	
162	<!-- Versions web-verified 2026-10-26; the project's pubspec.yaml owns the exact pin once F000 scaffolds it. -->
163	
164	| Name | Version |
165	| --- | --- |
166	| Flutter SDK | 3.47.x stable family (pin the exact patch via `fvm` at F000 time) |
167	| flutter_bloc | ^9.1.1 |
168	| go_router | ^18.1.1 |
169	| dio | ^5.11.1 |
170	| hive_ce + hive_ce_flutter | ^2.22.0 |
171	| get_it | ^9.3.0 |
172	| fpdart | ^1.2.0 |
173	| freezed + freezed_annotation | ^4.0.3 |
174	| json_serializable | ^6.15.2 |
175	| build_runner | latest compatible with the pinned Dart SDK |
176	| mocktail | ^1.0.5 |
177	| fl_chart | ^1.3.0 |
178	| local_auth | ^3.0.2 |
179	| flutter_secure_storage | ^11.2.0 |
180	| flutter_dotenv | ^6.0.1 |
181	| whisper_ggml | ^2.8.1 |
182	
183	## Structural Seed

# Architecture Spine — Cerne

## Design Paradigm

**Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature, BLoC on top, errors carried as values.**

- `presentation/` (BLoC/Cubit + widgets) → depends on → `domain/` (entities, use cases, repository/port interfaces) ← implemented by ← `data/` (DTOs, data sources, repository implementations).
- `domain/` is the only layer every other layer may depend on; it depends on nothing feature-specific and never on `package:flutter` (RNF06).
- Every operation that can fail (network, parse, local I/O) returns `Either<Failure, T>` (`fpdart`) at the repository boundary — no repository throws past itself (RNF09).
- `core/` sits beneath every feature and holds the only cross-feature-shared code: the `Failure` hierarchy, the API client/URL builder, the DI bootstrap, the local-cache boxes, `Resource<T>`, `isolatedSideEffect`, design tokens, and the `SessionStatus` contract.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Feature["any lib/features/<name>/"]
        P["presentation (BLoC/Cubit, widgets)"]
        D["domain (entities, use cases, port interfaces)"]
        DA["data (DTOs, data sources, repository impl)"]
        P --> D
        DA --> D
    end
    Core["core/ (Failure, ApiClient, DI, cache, Resource<T>, SessionStatus, VaultStatus, design_tokens)"]
    D --> Core
    DA --> Core
    OtherDomain["another feature's domain/ (port interfaces only)"]
    P -.->|"AD-6: cross-feature calls only through the owning feature's domain port"| OtherDomain
```

## Invariants & Rules

### AD-1 — Layer dependency direction (RNF06)

- **Binds:** all features
- **Prevents:** `domain/` depending on Flutter, on any `data/` (own or another feature's), or on another feature's `presentation/`.
- **Rule:** dependency direction is strictly `presentation → domain ← data`. `domain/` imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything under any `data/`. Only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins. `presentation/` never imports a feature's own or another feature's `data/` directly.

### AD-2 — Either-everywhere error channel (RNF09)

- **Binds:** all repositories (read and write)
- **Prevents:** a feature inventing its own error signaling (exceptions crossing the repository boundary, nullable returns, ad hoc string errors) that other code can't pattern-match generically.
- **Rule:** every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream). `Failure` is the closed hierarchy in AD-3. No repository implementation lets a native/dio exception escape unmapped.

### AD-3 — Closed `Failure` hierarchy `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** all
- **Prevents:** two features inventing different shapes for "network timeout," or silently dropping one of the server's 13 codes.
- **Rule:** one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes — the 13 from `error-taxonomy.md` (`AuthExpired`, `AuthInvalid`, `NetworkTimeout`, `NetworkOffline`, `Validation`, `PiiCheckFailed`, `EmbeddingFailed`, `AiGenerationTimeout`, `NotFound`, `RateLimited`, `ExportEmptyPeriod`, `PayloadTooLarge`, `OcrNoText`) plus the local-only `MalformedResponse` (`retryable` hardcoded `false`, for the client's own parse-failure detection). Never redefined or subset per feature. `AuthInvalid` can only ever originate from `POST /auth/login` — no biometric/PIN check ever reaches the server (AD-14), so no feature maps a local vault failure to this code.

### AD-4 — Retry policy lives in exactly one place `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** the API client
- **Prevents:** a feature writing its own retry loop that double-retries, or retries a `retryable:false` code.
- **Rule:** retry logic is implemented once (the `dio` interceptor / `ApiClient` wrapper), fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes (`NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_OFFLINE`, `PII_CHECK_FAILED`, `EMBEDDING_FAILED`, `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMITED`). Every other code surfaces once, unretried.

### AD-5 — Function-name URL construction and header policy

- **Binds:** every network call
- **Prevents:** a feature string-concatenating the literal `openapi.yaml` REST path (which is not a real URL) or re-deciding which `Authorization` value to send.
- **Rule:** one URL builder in `core/` maps each operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>`. One `dio` interceptor owns headers: `apikey` on every call; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` only on the three `security: []` operations (signup, login, refresh); `Authorization: Bearer <user token>` on every other (`bearerAuth`) operation.

### AD-6 — `entries` owns `Entry` from RF01 onward; every other feature reaches it only through a domain-layer port

- **Binds:** RF01 (capture → entries, the *first* consumer — delivery order builds RF01 three units before RF06/RF07), RF10 (chat → entries), and any future cross-feature dependency
- **Prevents:** (a) RF01 inventing its own local `Entry` model/repository/cache box because `features/entries/` "doesn't exist yet" at its position in the delivery order, which RF06/RF07 would then duplicate; (b) any feature reaching into `entries`'s `data/`, repository, data source, or BLoC — the exact violation RF10's acceptance criteria calls out, which would also break RNF06.
- **Rule:** `features/entries/` is scaffolded at RF01 (not RF06/RF07) because RF01 is the first unit that must call `POST /entries` (requirements.md §6.2). From RF01 on, `entries/domain` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create`, `read` — see AD-11), and the entries Hive box. `entries` exposes an abstract `CreateEntryUseCase`/`SaveEntryUseCase`-shaped port; RF01's `capture` feature and RF10's `chat` feature are both *consumers* — each only ever imports and injects that abstract type from `entries/domain`, never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`. RF06/RF07 extend the same `EntriesRepository` port with `list`/`search` methods; they do not introduce a second entry model or a second owner. The port's `create` is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`: a second call for a `chatMessageId` that already has an entry never creates a duplicate — the implementation (not the port's type signature) is responsible for this check, binding on RF10's build.

### AD-7 — No BLoC-to-BLoC references

- **Binds:** all (generalizes RF07's explicit AC to every feature)
- **Prevents:** hidden coupling and circular-rebuild chains between presentation units built independently.
- **Rule:** a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency, same-feature or cross-feature. Composition of multiple independent state sources happens by injecting the underlying `domain/` streams/use-cases into each BLoC independently, or via `BlocListener`/`MultiBlocListener` in the widget tree — never a direct BLoC → BLoC reference.

### AD-8 — Single `SessionStatus` source of truth

- **Binds:** F000 (go_router redirect), RF07 (composite auth × sync × data state), any feature that needs session validity
- **Prevents:** two independently-built screens disagreeing on what "session expired" means or when to prompt re-login.
- **Rule:** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream, exposed from the auth feature's `domain/`, registered once in DI as a singleton. Every consumer injects/listens to that stream; none re-derives session state from a raw 401, from its own `GET /auth/session` poll, or from a second stream. `SessionStatus` governs *server session validity only* — it composes with the local vault gate per AD-14, it does not replace it.

### AD-9 — Cloud-only: no offline write queue

- **Binds:** all repositories (generalizes RF06's "cloud-only" note and RF04's "blocked offline" writes)
- **Prevents:** a feature building a local write-queue/outbox that silently diverges from "offline permits viewing cached data only."
- **Rule:** a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)` — it is never queued for later. Plain reads (`GET /entries`, `GET /chat/sessions`, `GET .../messages`) transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache. **Semantic search is the one read exception:** `GET /entries/search` has no client-side vector index to fall back to, so with no connectivity it also resolves to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)`, same as a write — it is never served from cache. The only client-side "pending write" state is transient, in-memory, scoped to one in-flight request (it feeds AD-10's `Synchronizing` badge state) — it is never persisted as a queue.

### AD-10 — Sync badge is a pure client-side derivation (locks `sync-badge.md`)

- **Binds:** every screen that renders the per-entry sync badge (chat save confirmation, My Records list, any future one)
- **Prevents:** two screens computing `Synchronizing`/`Error`/`Synchronized` differently.
- **Rule:** one derivation function lives in `entries/domain`, computed from three inputs: `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and the transient per-entry write state (AD-9) — which is itself one of three values: no pending write (→ `Synchronized`), a write in flight (→ `Synchronizing`), or the in-flight write's `Future` resolved to `Left(Failure)` (→ `Synchronization error`, held until the next write attempt reconciles it). Every screen consumes that function's output; none recomputes the badge inline. The server never supplies a `sync_status` field — `requirements.md` §8 is wrong on this point (`sync-badge.md` and the `Entry` schema win).

### AD-11 — Entry immutability

- **Binds:** the entries feature
- **Prevents:** a unit speculatively adding an update/delete path the backend doesn't support.
- **Rule:** `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read operations only. No update or delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`.

### AD-12 — Shared view-state scoped to single-source-of-truth fetches `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** RF06 (search results), RF09 (dashboard aggregate/narrative) — explicitly *not* RF02, RF04, or RF07
- **Prevents:** forcing a composite or multi-stage state machine into a generic fetch enum, and the reverse: ad hoc one-off state shapes where a shared one would do.
- **Rule:** generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) lives in `core/`, used only by screens with one data source and one fetch lifecycle. RF02's capture pipeline (`recording`/`processing`/`transcribed`/`error`), RF07's composite auth × sync × data state, and RF04's chat message stream (append-only, streaming/SSE, not a single fetch) each define their own sealed state class — never forced into `Resource<T>`. RF08's proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto RF04's existing chat state, not a parallel `Resource<T>`.

### AD-13 — `isolatedSideEffect` contract fixed now, implementation deferred `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** RF08, RF10 (both state the identical failure-isolation requirement)
- **Prevents:** RF08 reinventing its own failure-isolation wrapper (or importing RF10's feature-local one), producing two incompatible "never block the caller on failure" implementations.
- **Rule:** `core/` holds a never-throws helper with signature `Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped (never throws past itself); it ships with RF10, delivery order's first consumer (RF04 → RF10 → RF08), not built speculatively in F000. The helper's own `Future` always completes independently of the caller: RF10 may `await` it before updating its button state, and RF08 must be able to call it **without** awaiting (fire-and-forget) so a slow/failed insight generation never blocks or delays the chat stream. RF08 reuses it from `core/` without a cross-feature import.

### AD-14 — One `go_router` redirect composes exactly two gates, in a fixed order: vault, then session

- **Binds:** F000 (builds the redirect skeleton + `SessionStatus` half), RF03 (plugs the vault half into the same redirect)
- **Prevents:** F000 and RF03 each building an independent navigation gate (two competing `redirect` callbacks, or RF03 bolting a second check onto screens individually) — `go_router` supports only one top-level `redirect`, so two independently-built gates cannot both "just work."
- **Rule:** the redirect composes exactly two domain-level streams, evaluated in this order: (1) `VaultStatus` (local-only — biometric/PIN unlocked, Face-ID-failed-offer-PIN, or locked after the 5-minute background timeout; RF03 exposes it from `features/vault/domain` the same way auth exposes `SessionStatus`, AD-8) — checked *first*, before any network state, because it gates whether the app may show anything at all; then (2) `SessionStatus` (AD-8) once the vault is unlocked. Neither gate ever reaches the server to validate itself (`POST /auth/login` is the only path that can produce `AuthInvalid`, per AD-3) — the vault is validated entirely on-device, consistent with the backend having no biometric-unlock endpoint.

### AD-15 — The local cache is a projection, never a query engine

- **Binds:** `entries`, `chat` — every feature with a `hive_ce` box `[ADOPTED, promoted from the F000 forge session]`
- **Prevents:** a unit adding local filtering, joining, or sorting logic "for performance" or "for offline support," which would then disagree with the server's own filter semantics (AD-9's offline read rule assumes the cache's content is a verbatim copy, not a re-derived view).
- **Rule:** every query dimension (`source`, `dateFrom`/`dateTo`, semantic search, pagination cursor) is a server-side query parameter per `openapi.yaml`. A `hive_ce` box stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id (or by session id for messages); no feature ever filters, joins, sorts, or re-derives a different view from a cached collection — a cache miss or a dimension not covered by AD-9's offline-read rule surfaces `Failure.networkOffline`, it is never approximated locally.

## Consistency Conventions

| Concern | Convention |
| --- | --- |
| Feature naming | `lib/features/<feature>/` one of: `auth`, `vault`, `capture`, `entries`, `chat`, `export`, `dashboard`, `account` — see Capability → Architecture Map |
| Errors | `Failure` sealed hierarchy (AD-3) everywhere; UI maps a `Failure` to copy using its `retryable` flag, never a hardcoded per-screen message list |
| IDs & dates | server-assigned string IDs and ISO-8601 timestamps passed through verbatim from DTOs (`freezed`+`json_serializable`); the client never generates or reformats an entity ID |
| Visual values | `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` only (RNF08) — no color/font/spacing/radius literal anywhere else |
| Network envelope | one `ApiClient`/URL-builder + one header interceptor (AD-5); no feature constructs a request URL or header set itself |
| State composition | `Resource<T>` for single-source fetches (AD-12); no BLoC-to-BLoC references (AD-7) |
| Testing | `mocktail` stubs one `ApiClient` interface per repository test, not a fake transport layer; one shared table-driven helper drives the 5-write-endpoints × 3-failure-types = 15-scenario matrix (RNF09); ≥80% line coverage gate on every `domain/` (RNF07) |
| Config/secrets | `.env` (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) loaded via `flutter_dotenv` `[ASSUMPTION — settled here; requirements.md left it "free," no prior session decided it]`; never committed, never hardcoded |
| AI provider access | the app never calls Claude or Voyage AI directly — every AI-backed feature goes through the backend's documented endpoints (project policy, binding on all features) |
| Local cache | `hive_ce` boxes are a projection of server responses, never a query engine (AD-15) |
| Pagination/cursor | every paginated list (`entries`, `entries/search`, `chat_sessions`, `chat_messages`) uses the server's own cursor convention verbatim; the cursor string is cached alongside the box it pages (AD-15) — `entries` and `entries/search` share one cursor convention since both live in the one `entries` feature (AD-6) |
| Fixed numeric parameters (`requirements.md` §10 — not reinterpretable) | background session timeout 5 min (RF03) · search debounce 300 ms (RF06) · proactive-insight trigger N=5 user messages OR T=2 min inactivity, fires once per satisfied condition (RF08) · dashboard rendering scenarios 0 / 1 / >30 entries (RF09) · local UI latency <100 ms, loading indicator threshold >300 ms (RNF01) · domain coverage ≥80% (RNF07) · 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types = 15 scenarios (RNF09) — each is implemented inside its owning feature (not a shared core constant), but none may be approximated or re-tuned by whichever unit builds it |

## Stack

| F000 — scaffold, tokens, HTTP client, auth, base nav | `core/`, `features/auth/` | AD-1..AD-5, AD-8, AD-14 (session half) |
| RF03 — biometric/PIN vault | `features/vault/` | AD-14 (vault half), AD-3 (`AuthInvalid` note) |
| RF01 — multimodal capture | `features/capture/` → `features/entries/` (introduces it) | AD-1, AD-2, AD-6, AD-9, AD-15 |
| RF02 — STT/OCR processing | `features/capture/` | AD-12 (excluded — own state machine) |
| RF07 — multi-source history (timeline) | `features/entries/` (extends with timeline read) | AD-7, AD-8, AD-10, AD-12 (excluded), AD-15 |
| RF06 — semantic search/filter | `features/entries/` (extends with search) | AD-9 (search carve-out), AD-12, AD-15 |
| RF04 — chat with memory (RAG) | `features/chat/` | AD-1, AD-2, AD-9, AD-12 (own stream, excluded) |
| RF10 — save chat message as entry | `features/chat/` → `features/entries/` | AD-6 (idempotency), AD-13 |
| RF08 — proactive insights | `features/chat/` | AD-12 (overlay on chat state), AD-13 (fire-and-forget) |
| RF05 — personal summary export | `features/export/` | AD-1, AD-2 |
| RF09 — temporal summaries/dashboard | `features/dashboard/` | AD-12 |
| RNF05 — account deletion, settings | `features/account/` | AD-1, AD-2 |

## Deferred

- **Epic/story breakdown within each build unit** — this spine fixes cross-unit invariants, not per-story task sequencing; owned by `bmad-create-epics-and-stories`.
- **CI/CD pipeline and release process** — no CI tool, test-runner wiring, or App Store distribution step is specified anywhere in the input package, and no project deadline is stated (flagged as an open PRD question). Revisit once a submission/demo deadline exists.
- **Exact fvm-pinned Flutter/Dart patch and the real `flutter test`/`flutter analyze` invocations** — `AGENTS.md`'s "Running and verifying" section leaves these open until F000 scaffolds the project; this spine names the current stable family (3.47.x), not a committed patch.
- **Persona system-prompt wiring and manual-tag UI behavior** — both are explicit extension features (`requirements.md` §2) that receive no functional implementation; no architecture owns their logic.
- **Dashboard cache-invalidation behavior (RF09 AC)** — a presentation-layer concern for whichever unit builds RF09, not a local-cache architecture decision.
- **Combined search + filter interaction semantics** when both a search term and date/source filters are active — flagged as an open PRD question (blocks RF06); `requirements.md` §6 fixes AND-logic between two *filters*, but search-term-plus-filter combination is still open. Resolve at RF06 build time, not here.
- **Product-level open questions carried from the PRD, not resolved here because they're not architecture-level:** signup field set (password confirmation / display name — blocks F000), tab-switching mid-capture in the Insertion Modal (discard/warn/persist — blocks RF01), whether the sync-badge error state needs a visible retry affordance or reconciliation-on-next-write is sufficient (blocks RF07). None of the three changes an AD in this spine regardless of how they're answered; each is a product decision for the unit that builds it.
- **Integration spike flagged, not yet run:** `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` have not been verified working together in one scaffold (each is independently current per the Stack table, but their combination at F000's bootstrap time is unverified). Run this as the first thing F000 does, before building on top of it.

200	
201	> **[ASSUMPTION]** Color/typography/spacing/radius token *names* intentionally mirror `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` section 3 verbatim (camelCase, not the spec's conventional kebab-case) rather than being re-cased, so this file maps 1:1 to the eventual `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` constants with zero translation step. Elevation values are inlined as literal shadow strings inside `components` (matching `elevation1`/`elevation2` below) rather than cross-referenced, since the DESIGN.md spec's frontmatter token categories don't include an `elevation` path.
202	
203	## Brand & Style
204	
205	Cerne reads as a paper journal, not a productivity tool. The palette is forest-and-ink: a deep green (`colorPrimary`, `#1F3D34`) anchors every structural surface — app bar, primary buttons, wordmark — the color of a leather journal cover, not a corporate brand blue. The canvas underneath (`colorSurfaceBg` `#F2EFE7`, `colorSurfaceElevated` `#FBF9F4`) is warm paper, never clinical white. One accent — ochre (`colorAccent`, `#C98A3E`) — is the single chromatic signal in the entire system, reserved for the three moments the product wants the user to notice: a proactive insight, a saved bookmark, a primary call-to-action. Everything else stays in the green/paper/ink register.
206	
207	Typography carries the same editorial intent: `Fraunces` (a serif with visible character) is reserved for the two moments that deserve weight — the splash wordmark and section headlines — while `Karla` (a clean grotesque) carries every working UI surface, and `IBM Plex Mono` marks anything that is data rather than prose (timestamps, counters, status labels), the way a ledger distinguishes dates from narrative.
208	
209	The product is explicitly **not** a mental-health or clinical tool (`docs/input/requirements.md` RF05, known-limitation note). Nothing in the visual system should borrow clinical signifiers — no stethoscope-blue, no checklist-green, no alarmist red beyond the one error token used sparingly. The identity is "quiet companion with a notebook," not "app for a diagnosis."
210	
211	## Colors
212	
213	- **`colorPrimary` / `colorPrimaryPressed`** — the structural green. App bar, primary buttons, the splash wordmark. Pressed state is a darker shade of the same hue, never a different color — reinforces "same surface, pushed in."
214	- **`colorOnPrimary`** — warm off-white text/icon color on any green surface. Never pure white.
215	- **`colorAccent` / `colorOnAccent`** — ochre, the system's only decorative color. Used exclusively for: the insight-card spine, the saved-bookmark check, and primary CTAs that need to stand out from the structural green (e.g., "Baixar PDF"). Never used for navigation, never for more than one element on screen at a time.
216	- **`colorSecondary`** — sage green. Tags, chips, the "synchronizing" badge dot. A quieter, desaturated cousin of the primary — present but not asking for attention.
217	- **`colorSurfaceBg` / `colorSurfaceElevated`** — two tones of warm paper. `Bg` is the canvas; `Elevated` is anything that sits on top of it (cards, bubbles, sheets) — the only separation device besides `elevation1`/`elevation2`, never a hard border.
218	- **`colorBorder`** — the only line-weight gray. Dividers, input borders, disabled-button fill. Kept at low contrast on purpose — a divider is punctuation, not a wall.
219	- **`colorTextPrimary` / `colorTextSecondary`** — ink, full and half-strength. Primary for anything the user wrote or needs to read; secondary for metadata and supporting text.
220	- **`colorError`** — a muted brick red, not a siren red. Used for destructive actions, validation, and failure states — but deliberately desaturated to avoid an alarmist tone in a journaling context.
221	- **`colorSuccess`** — reuses the sage-adjacent dark green family for "synchronized" and confirmations. Success is quiet, not celebratory (no bright green, no confetti-adjacent hue).
222	- **`colorWarningSync`** — literally the same hex as `colorAccent`. The "synchronizing" badge intentionally borrows the accent rather than introducing a fourth warm hue — a transient, benign state shares the visual register of "something good is happening," not alarm.
223	- **`colorInfoOffline`** — a single-use blue-gray, the only cool color in the system. Reserved for the offline banner alone, so its appearance is unambiguous: this color means "no connection," nowhere else.
224	- **`colorChatBubbleUser`** — a pale sage, distinguishing the user's own words from the AI's ivory bubble without introducing a new hue family.
225	
226	**Avoid:** using `colorError` for anything short of a real failure — the muted tone depends on rarity to still read as serious. (Accent/offline-color misuse and the extension-screen placeholder rule are covered once, in **Do's and Don'ts**, rather than restated here.)
227	
228	## Typography
229	
230	Two families carry meaning; the third carries data:
231	
232	- **`Fraunces`** (`textDisplayLg`, `textHeadlineMd`) — the only serif, the only place personality shows through letterforms. Splash wordmark and section titles only. Never body text, never a button label.
233	- **`Karla`** (`textTitleLg` through `textLabelMd`) — every working surface: app-bar titles, chat bubbles, entries, buttons, chips, descriptions. The weight ramp (700 → 400 → 500) carries hierarchy, not size alone.
234	- **`IBM Plex Mono`** (`textMonoCaption`) — exclusively technical metadata: timestamps, audio counters ("00:12"), sync-status labels. Monospace reads as "machine-reported fact," which is exactly the register a timestamp or a counter should carry, distinct from anything the user or the AI composed.
235	
236	Dynamic type is honored at every level (see **Accessibility Floor** in `EXPERIENCE.md`) — no UI value is hardcoded outside `design_tokens.dart` per RNF08, and no control should truncate or clip at the largest accessibility text size.
237	
238	## Layout & Spacing
239	
240	4dp grid throughout: `spacingXs` (4) for the tightest relationships (icon-to-label), up to `spacing2xl` (48) between fully unrelated sections. Frame is fixed at 390×844 logical points, portrait only, single column — there is no tablet or landscape layout to reconcile against (`docs/input/requirements.md` section 13: "Platform: iOS, portrait only").
241	
242	Overlays stack **at most one level deep**: a bottom sheet or dialog sits on a darkened scrim over exactly one base screen (Home/Chat, Meus Registros, or Configurações). No overlay opens another overlay on top of itself — the insertion modal's three tabs are internal states of one sheet, not nested sheets.
243	
244	## Elevation & Depth
245	
246	Two tokens only, both soft and low-contrast — this is a paper surface, not a glossy one:
247	
248	- **`elevation1`** — `0 1px 3px rgba(36,31,25,.08)`. Resting cards, chat bubbles, record cards. A hint of lift, nothing dramatic.
249	- **`elevation2`** — `0 4px 16px rgba(36,31,25,.14)`. Sheets and modals only — the one visual cue, together with the scrim, that something is temporarily on top of the normal flow.
250	
251	Nothing else carries elevation. Hierarchy between a card and its background comes primarily from the `colorSurfaceBg` / `colorSurfaceElevated` tonal step, with shadow as a secondary, minimal reinforcement.
252	
253	## Shapes
254	
255	- **`radiusSm`** (8dp) — inputs, chips. The smallest, most utilitarian corner.
256	- **`radiusMd`** (16dp) — cards, chat bubbles. Each bubble additionally squares off exactly one corner (bottom-right for the user, bottom-left for the AI) — the one place the system breaks a uniform radius, as the deliberate speech-bubble "tail" substitute.
257	- **`radiusLg`** (24dp) — sheets and modals — the largest radius, reinforcing "this is a different layer of the UI," paired with `elevation2`.
258	- **`radiusFull`** (999dp) — avatars and pills (filter chips) only.
259	
260	## Components
261	
262	- **Buttons** — primary (filled `colorPrimary`, darkens to `colorPrimaryPressed`), secondary (outline, no fill, for "Tentar novamente" / "Cancelar" / "Baixar dados brutos"), text/ghost (no chrome at all, for mode-toggle links and "Fechar" / "Limpar"). Disabled state is always `colorBorder` background with `colorTextSecondary` text — never a dimmed opacity of the active state.
263	- **Chat bubbles** — user (sage, square bottom-right) vs. AI (ivory, `elevation1`, square bottom-left, shadow present because it sits on the paper canvas the same way a sticky note would). Streaming state adds a blinking cursor at the text's end; no other visual change while generating.
264	- **Insight card** — ochre spine on the left edge, mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x." The spine color is the only accent-colored element inside the chat stream — it must stand out against both bubble colors.
265	- **Bookmark button** — four states on every user message: idle (outline), saving (spinner), saved (ochre check — the second of the system's two accent uses), error (red warning). State is carried by icon + color together, never color alone (see Accessibility Floor).
266	- **Record card** — spine colored by origin: manual = `colorPrimary` (dark green), audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = `colorAccent`. The spine is the *only* place color encodes a data dimension (entry source) rather than a UI state — keep it that way; don't reuse spine coloring logic for anything else.
267	- **Sync badge** — a small dot, not a pill or label by default: green/ochre/red for synced/synchronizing/error. Color is reinforced by an accessible label on tap or long-focus (see Accessibility Floor) since dot color alone is not sufficient signal.
268	- **Filter chip** — sage background, dark-olive text (`colorOnCategoryChip`), fully rounded. Single-choice (date range) and multi-choice (category, type) look identical; the difference is behavioral, not visual (see `EXPERIENCE.md`).
269	- **Search bar** — paper-elevated input with a trailing funnel icon button; same visual family as `text-field` but permanently docked at the top of Meus Registros, never submitted with a button.
270	- **Filter sheet** — a `radiusLg`/`elevation2` sheet, same surface language as any other bottom sheet; groups are labeled in `textMonoCaption` (treated as metadata about the list, not prose).
271	- **Tab bar** (insertion modal) — three equal-width segments; the active segment alone gets a filled `colorPrimary` background, the other two stay transparent with secondary-colored text.
272	- **Audio waveform** — animated bars in the structural palette while recording; frozen at 35% opacity while processing — the opacity drop alone communicates "this is no longer live," no additional label needed over the "Transcrevendo..." text.
273	- **Avatar** — solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials in `colorOnPrimary`, two fixed sizes (40px menu, 52px Settings). No photo avatars anywhere in the product. In Configurações, the pencil icon beside the editable name/e-mail becomes a check icon in edit mode — the only place an icon itself changes meaning rather than just color.
274	- **PIN keypad** — numeric 3×4 grid + backspace, progress dots above, all in the structural palette (no accent color on digits).
275	- **Export sheet** — the heaviest surface after a full-screen modal (`radiusLg` + `elevation2`), since it carries a multi-stage async job.
276	- **Confirmation dialog** — neutral title (`colorTextPrimary`) for session expiry, red title (`colorError`) for destructive deletion — the title color is the only signal distinguishing "routine interruption" from "irreversible action," so it must never be muted.
277	- **Skeleton** — shown only past the 300ms loading-indicator threshold (RNF01); appears as a `colorBorder`-toned shimmer, never a spinner, for content (not action) loading.
278	
279	## Do's and Don'ts
280	
281	| Do | Don't |
282	|---|---|
283	| Keep `colorAccent` to its two canonical uses (insight spine, saved bookmark) plus primary CTAs that need emphasis | Use the accent decoratively, or add a second chromatic accent |
284	| Pull every color/type/space/radius value from `design_tokens.dart` (RNF08) | Hardcode a hex, font size, or dp value anywhere in a widget |
285	| Style extension screens (Planos de Ação, persona cards) with full visual polish | Mark unimplemented features with a visibly "unfinished" or grayed-out treatment |
286	| Pair every state color with an icon or label (bookmark, sync badge) | Encode state (saved / error / synchronizing) in color alone |
287	| Keep `Fraunces` for display/headline only | Set body text, buttons, or labels in `Fraunces` |
288	| Treat `colorInfoOffline` as single-use (offline banner only) | Reuse the offline blue-gray for any other informational banner |
289	| Ship one light theme, faithful to the prototype's single palette | Add a dark-mode variant not present in the frozen Design Tokens panel |
290
