    radius: '{rounded.radiusFull}'
    sizeMenu: 40px
    sizeSettings: 52px
  export-sheet:
    background: '{colors.colorSurfaceElevated}'
    radius: '{rounded.radiusLg}'
    elevation: 0 4px 16px rgba(36,31,25,.14)
  confirmation-dialog:
    background: '{colors.colorSurfaceElevated}'
    scrim: rgba(36,31,25,.4)
    radius: '{rounded.radiusLg}'
    titleNeutral: '{colors.colorTextPrimary}'
    titleDestructive: '{colors.colorError}'
  skeleton:
    background: '{colors.colorBorder}'
    shimmer: '{colors.colorSurfaceElevated}'
    showAfter: 300ms
---

> **[ASSUMPTION]** Color/typography/spacing/radius token *names* intentionally mirror `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` section 3 verbatim (camelCase, not the spec's conventional kebab-case) rather than being re-cased, so this file maps 1:1 to the eventual `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` constants with zero translation step. Elevation values are inlined as literal shadow strings inside `components` (matching `elevation1`/`elevation2` below) rather than cross-referenced, since the DESIGN.md spec's frontmatter token categories don't include an `elevation` path.

## Brand & Style

Cerne reads as a paper journal, not a productivity tool. The palette is forest-and-ink: a deep green (`colorPrimary`, `#1F3D34`) anchors every structural surface — app bar, primary buttons, wordmark — the color of a leather journal cover, not a corporate brand blue. The canvas underneath (`colorSurfaceBg` `#F2EFE7`, `colorSurfaceElevated` `#FBF9F4`) is warm paper, never clinical white. One accent — ochre (`colorAccent`, `#C98A3E`) — is the single chromatic signal in the entire system, reserved for the three moments the product wants the user to notice: a proactive insight, a saved bookmark, a primary call-to-action. Everything else stays in the green/paper/ink register.

Typography carries the same editorial intent: `Fraunces` (a serif with visible character) is reserved for the two moments that deserve weight — the splash wordmark and section headlines — while `Karla` (a clean grotesque) carries every working UI surface, and `IBM Plex Mono` marks anything that is data rather than prose (timestamps, counters, status labels), the way a ledger distinguishes dates from narrative.

The product is explicitly **not** a mental-health or clinical tool (`docs/input/requirements.md` RF05, known-limitation note). Nothing in the visual system should borrow clinical signifiers — no stethoscope-blue, no checklist-green, no alarmist red beyond the one error token used sparingly. The identity is "quiet companion with a notebook," not "app for a diagnosis."

## Colors

- **`colorPrimary` / `colorPrimaryPressed`** — the structural green. App bar, primary buttons, the splash wordmark. Pressed state is a darker shade of the same hue, never a different color — reinforces "same surface, pushed in."
- **`colorOnPrimary`** — warm off-white text/icon color on any green surface. Never pure white.
- **`colorAccent` / `colorOnAccent`** — ochre, the system's only decorative color. Used exclusively for: the insight-card spine, the saved-bookmark check, and primary CTAs that need to stand out from the structural green (e.g., "Baixar PDF"). Never used for navigation, never for more than one element on screen at a time.
- **`colorSecondary`** — sage green. Tags, chips, the "synchronizing" badge dot. A quieter, desaturated cousin of the primary — present but not asking for attention.
- **`colorSurfaceBg` / `colorSurfaceElevated`** — two tones of warm paper. `Bg` is the canvas; `Elevated` is anything that sits on top of it (cards, bubbles, sheets) — the only separation device besides `elevation1`/`elevation2`, never a hard border.
- **`colorBorder`** — the only line-weight gray. Dividers, input borders, disabled-button fill. Kept at low contrast on purpose — a divider is punctuation, not a wall.
- **`colorTextPrimary` / `colorTextSecondary`** — ink, full and half-strength. Primary for anything the user wrote or needs to read; secondary for metadata and supporting text.
- **`colorError`** — a muted brick red, not a siren red. Used for destructive actions, validation, and failure states — but deliberately desaturated to avoid an alarmist tone in a journaling context.
- **`colorSuccess`** — reuses the sage-adjacent dark green family for "synchronized" and confirmations. Success is quiet, not celebratory (no bright green, no confetti-adjacent hue).
- **`colorWarningSync`** — literally the same hex as `colorAccent`. The "synchronizing" badge intentionally borrows the accent rather than introducing a fourth warm hue — a transient, benign state shares the visual register of "something good is happening," not alarm.
- **`colorInfoOffline`** — a single-use blue-gray, the only cool color in the system. Reserved for the offline banner alone, so its appearance is unambiguous: this color means "no connection," nowhere else.
- **`colorChatBubbleUser`** — a pale sage, distinguishing the user's own words from the AI's ivory bubble without introducing a new hue family.

**Avoid:** using `colorError` for anything short of a real failure — the muted tone depends on rarity to still read as serious. (Accent/offline-color misuse and the extension-screen placeholder rule are covered once, in **Do's and Don'ts**, rather than restated here.)

## Typography

Two families carry meaning; the third carries data:

- **`Fraunces`** (`textDisplayLg`, `textHeadlineMd`) — the only serif, the only place personality shows through letterforms. Splash wordmark and section titles only. Never body text, never a button label.
- **`Karla`** (`textTitleLg` through `textLabelMd`) — every working surface: app-bar titles, chat bubbles, entries, buttons, chips, descriptions. The weight ramp (700 → 400 → 500) carries hierarchy, not size alone.
- **`IBM Plex Mono`** (`textMonoCaption`) — exclusively technical metadata: timestamps, audio counters ("00:12"), sync-status labels. Monospace reads as "machine-reported fact," which is exactly the register a timestamp or a counter should carry, distinct from anything the user or the AI composed.

Dynamic type is honored at every level (see **Accessibility Floor** in `EXPERIENCE.md`) — no UI value is hardcoded outside `design_tokens.dart` per RNF08, and no control should truncate or clip at the largest accessibility text size.

## Layout & Spacing

4dp grid throughout: `spacingXs` (4) for the tightest relationships (icon-to-label), up to `spacing2xl` (48) between fully unrelated sections. Frame is fixed at 390×844 logical points, portrait only, single column — there is no tablet or landscape layout to reconcile against (`docs/input/requirements.md` section 13: "Platform: iOS, portrait only").

Overlays stack **at most one level deep**: a bottom sheet or dialog sits on a darkened scrim over exactly one base screen (Home/Chat, Meus Registros, or Configurações). No overlay opens another overlay on top of itself — the insertion modal's three tabs are internal states of one sheet, not nested sheets.

## Elevation & Depth

Two tokens only, both soft and low-contrast — this is a paper surface, not a glossy one:

- **`elevation1`** — `0 1px 3px rgba(36,31,25,.08)`. Resting cards, chat bubbles, record cards. A hint of lift, nothing dramatic.
- **`elevation2`** — `0 4px 16px rgba(36,31,25,.14)`. Sheets and modals only — the one visual cue, together with the scrim, that something is temporarily on top of the normal flow.

Nothing else carries elevation. Hierarchy between a card and its background comes primarily from the `colorSurfaceBg` / `colorSurfaceElevated` tonal step, with shadow as a secondary, minimal reinforcement.

## Shapes

- **`radiusSm`** (8dp) — inputs, chips. The smallest, most utilitarian corner.
- **`radiusMd`** (16dp) — cards, chat bubbles. Each bubble additionally squares off exactly one corner (bottom-right for the user, bottom-left for the AI) — the one place the system breaks a uniform radius, as the deliberate speech-bubble "tail" substitute.
- **`radiusLg`** (24dp) — sheets and modals — the largest radius, reinforcing "this is a different layer of the UI," paired with `elevation2`.
- **`radiusFull`** (999dp) — avatars and pills (filter chips) only.

## Components

- **Buttons** — primary (filled `colorPrimary`, darkens to `colorPrimaryPressed`), secondary (outline, no fill, for "Tentar novamente" / "Cancelar" / "Baixar dados brutos"), text/ghost (no chrome at all, for mode-toggle links and "Fechar" / "Limpar"). Disabled state is always `colorBorder` background with `colorTextSecondary` text — never a dimmed opacity of the active state.
- **Chat bubbles** — user (sage, square bottom-right) vs. AI (ivory, `elevation1`, square bottom-left, shadow present because it sits on the paper canvas the same way a sticky note would). Streaming state adds a blinking cursor at the text's end; no other visual change while generating.
- **Insight card** — ochre spine on the left edge, mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x." The spine color is the only accent-colored element inside the chat stream — it must stand out against both bubble colors.
- **Bookmark button** — four states on every user message: idle (outline), saving (spinner), saved (ochre check — the second of the system's two accent uses), error (red warning). State is carried by icon + color together, never color alone (see Accessibility Floor).
- **Record card** — spine colored by origin: manual = `colorPrimary` (dark green), audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = `colorAccent`. The spine is the *only* place color encodes a data dimension (entry source) rather than a UI state — keep it that way; don't reuse spine coloring logic for anything else.
- **Sync badge** — a small dot, not a pill or label by default: green/ochre/red for synced/synchronizing/error. Color is reinforced by an accessible label on tap or long-focus (see Accessibility Floor) since dot color alone is not sufficient signal.
- **Filter chip** — sage background, dark-olive text (`colorOnCategoryChip`), fully rounded. Single-choice (date range) and multi-choice (category, type) look identical; the difference is behavioral, not visual (see `EXPERIENCE.md`).
- **Search bar** — paper-elevated input with a trailing funnel icon button; same visual family as `text-field` but permanently docked at the top of Meus Registros, never submitted with a button.
- **Filter sheet** — a `radiusLg`/`elevation2` sheet, same surface language as any other bottom sheet; groups are labeled in `textMonoCaption` (treated as metadata about the list, not prose).
- **Tab bar** (insertion modal) — three equal-width segments; the active segment alone gets a filled `colorPrimary` background, the other two stay transparent with secondary-colored text.
- **Audio waveform** — animated bars in the structural palette while recording; frozen at 35% opacity while processing — the opacity drop alone communicates "this is no longer live," no additional label needed over the "Transcrevendo..." text.
- **Avatar** — solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials in `colorOnPrimary`, two fixed sizes (40px menu, 52px Settings). No photo avatars anywhere in the product. In Configurações, the pencil icon beside the editable name/e-mail becomes a check icon in edit mode — the only place an icon itself changes meaning rather than just color.
- **PIN keypad** — numeric 3×4 grid + backspace, progress dots above, all in the structural palette (no accent color on digits).
- **Export sheet** — the heaviest surface after a full-screen modal (`radiusLg` + `elevation2`), since it carries a multi-stage async job.
- **Confirmation dialog** — neutral title (`colorTextPrimary`) for session expiry, red title (`colorError`) for destructive deletion — the title color is the only signal distinguishing "routine interruption" from "irreversible action," so it must never be muted.
- **Skeleton** — shown only past the 300ms loading-indicator threshold (RNF01); appears as a `colorBorder`-toned shimmer, never a spinner, for content (not action) loading.

## Do's and Don'ts

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Keep `colorAccent` to its two canonical uses (insight spine, saved bookmark) plus primary CTAs that need emphasis | Use the accent decoratively, or add a second chromatic accent |
| Pull every color/type/space/radius value from `design_tokens.dart` (RNF08) | Hardcode a hex, font size, or dp value anywhere in a widget |
| Style extension screens (Planos de Ação, persona cards) with full visual polish | Mark unimplemented features with a visibly "unfinished" or grayed-out treatment |
| Pair every state color with an icon or label (bookmark, sync badge) | Encode state (saved / error / synchronizing) in color alone |
| Keep `Fraunces` for display/headline only | Set body text, buttons, or labels in `Fraunces` |
| Treat `colorInfoOffline` as single-use (offline banner only) | Reuse the offline blue-gray for any other informational banner |
| Ship one light theme, faithful to the prototype's single palette | Add a dark-mode variant not present in the frozen Design Tokens panel |

13	
14	# Cerne — Experience Spine
15	
16	> Single-surface mobile (iOS, portrait only). Paired with `DESIGN.md`. The product spec and visual prototype are frozen and unusually complete — this spine resolves the handful of gaps the spec explicitly leaves open (marked `[ASSUMPTION]`) rather than inventing new UX surface. `Responsive & Platform` is omitted: there is exactly one form factor (390×844pt, portrait, iOS only).
17	
18	## Foundation
19	
20	Single-surface mobile, iOS only, portrait only, 390×844 logical points. No third-party UI system — fully custom per `DESIGN.md` tokens, implemented with Flutter + `flutter_bloc` + Clean Architecture (`docs/input/requirements.md` section 9/13). Language: Portuguese, single locale, no i18n layer. `DESIGN.md` is the visual-identity reference; this file is the experience — behavior, states, interaction, accessibility, flows. Light mode only; there is no dark-mode or theme-switching surface (see `DESIGN.md` Do's and Don'ts).
21	
22	Three base screens hold almost everything; the rest are overlays on top of one of them, stacked at most one level deep:
23	
24	- **Home/Chat** — default landing after auth.
25	- **Meus Registros** — consolidated timeline.
26	- **Configurações** — profile, dashboard, account.
27	
28	## Information Architecture
29	
30	| Surface | Reached from | Purpose | Backend-gated by |
31	|---|---|---|---|
32	| Splash (Tela 0) | Cold app launch | Checks session + syncs cache in background, auto-advances (1.8s) | `GET /auth/session` |
33	| Biometria / PIN (Tela 0.1) | Splash, "Sair," account deletion | Local access barrier before any user data is exposed | device-local; `POST /auth/login` only if the session fully expired |
34	| Entrar / Criar conta (Tela 0.1a) | "usar e-mail e senha" link on Biometria | Fallback credential auth, same screen toggled by mode | `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/signup` |
35	| Home/Chat (Tela 1) | Auth success, "Novo Chat," back from any overlay | Continuous conversation with the AI, entry point to capture | `POST/GET /chat/sessions`, `.../messages` |
36	| Insertion Modal (Tela 2) | "+" on Home/Chat | Multimodal capture — text / audio / photo — each produces a persisted entry, never a chat message | `POST /entries`, `POST /media/ocr` |
37	| Side menu (Tela 3) | ☰ on Home/Chat | Navigation hub: session history, My Records / Action Plans / Settings, new conversation | `GET /chat/sessions` |
38	| Meus Registros (Tela 4) | Side menu | Timeline, filter, search, export | `GET /entries`, `GET /entries/search`, `POST/GET /export/...` |
39	| Planos de Ação (Tela 5) `[ext]` | Side menu | Static 3-column kanban, placeholder only — no functional implementation | none (no backend calls) |
40	| Configurações (Tela 6) | Side menu | Profile editing, evolution dashboard, persona toggle `[ext]`, logout, account deletion | `GET /dashboard/...`, `PATCH /account/settings`, `DELETE /account`, `POST /auth/logout` |
41	
42	No drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar — the side menu is the sole navigation hub besides the back arrow on Meus Registros and the "x" that closes any sheet/modal. Mirrors `docs/input/requirements.md` section 5.2 screen numbering and `prototype-extract.md` Tela numbering verbatim so both documents stay addressable by the same names.
43	
44	→ **Composition reference:** `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html` — the frozen prototype is itself the 1:1, interactive visual reference for all 32 navigable states (`prototype-extract.md` sections 1-2); no separate static mock is generated, since it must never change. Open it directly and navigate by `screen` state/overlay flag to see any surface this table names. Spine wins on conflict.
45	
46	## Voice and Tone
47	
48	Microcopy only — brand posture and aesthetic register live in `DESIGN.md.Brand & Style`. Default voice leans **empático** — warm, validating, never clinical. `[ASSUMPTION]`: the prototype's three persona options (Analítico / Empático / Socrático) are a non-functional cosmetic toggle (`docs/input/requirements.md` section 2), so the product must ship with exactly one real voice regardless of which card looks selected.
49	
50	| Do | Don't |
51	|---|---|
52	| "Não foi possível transcrever" / "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto" — exact prototype copy, factual, no blame | "Oops! Something went wrong 😢" |
53	| "Sessão expirada" with a plain explanation that history is kept | Any language implying data loss or starting over |
54	| Insight copy that surfaces a pattern ("parece que..., você mencionou...") without diagnosing or prescribing | Therapeutic framing, diagnostic language, or crisis-support claims — the product explicitly has no risk-signal protocol (`docs/input/requirements.md` section 4, known limitation) |
55	| "Resumo pronto" / "Baixar dados brutos" — plain, factual labels | Celebratory language around export or streaks around journaling frequency |
56	| Second person, direct ("Toque para desbloquear") | Infantilizing or over-familiar tone |
57	
58	## Component Patterns
59	
60	Behavioral; visual specs live in `DESIGN.md.Components`.
61	
62	| Component | Use | Behavioral rules |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| Insertion modal tab bar | Texto / Áudio / Foto | Opening the modal always resets all three tabs to idle/empty. Switching tabs while a capture is actively in flight (recording, or OCR/transcription processing) **cancels that capture outright** — no partial entry is created, applying RF01's existing cancel-on-interrupt rule to this trigger. `[ASSUMPTION]` (prototype leaves this undefined). |
65	| Chat bubble / message | Home/Chat | User bubbles are static once sent. AI bubbles alone carry a state machine: streaming (`{colors.colorTextPrimary}` text revealed progressively behind a blinking cursor) → complete, or → failure (timestamp slot replaced by red retry copy, bubble content never cleared). |
66	| Bookmark button (RF10) | Every user chat message | idle → saving → saved/error. Tapping an already-`saved` message is a no-op (idempotent per RF10 AC — same message never creates a duplicate entry). `error` returns to a retryable idle-like state, never stuck. Only user messages carry the button — AI responses never do. |
67	| Insight card (RF08) | Interleaved in chat | Fires once per satisfied trigger (5 user messages OR 2 min inactivity) — never both, never twice for the same window. Dismiss ("x") never changes scroll position or chat state. Failure to generate is silent to the user — chat continues uninterrupted. |
68	| Sync badge | Record card (Meus Registros) | Tap on an `error` badge (`{colors.colorError}` dot) retries that entry's write. `[ASSUMPTION]`, grounded in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`: the error means a local write was attempted and failed, so content is still held client-side and retry is meaningful. If the underlying error code is non-retryable (see State Patterns), show an inline explanation instead of a retry affordance. |
69	| Avatar — inline name editing | Configurações | Tapping the pencil beside the name/e-mail switches that field to an editable text input in place; the pencil icon becomes a check. Confirming commits via `PATCH /account/settings`; the field reverts to display mode either on save or on tapping elsewhere. No separate "edit profile" screen. |
70	| Record card | Meus Registros | Display-only — tapping a card does nothing beyond revealing its sync badge's retry affordance when in `error` state. No detail screen exists; entries are immutable, so no tap-to-edit or tap-to-expand behavior should be implied. |
71	| Search bar + filter sheet | Meus Registros | Query text and active filter chips combine with **AND** logic against the same `GET /entries/search` call — consistent with RF06's multi-filter AND rule. `[ASSUMPTION]` (prototype doesn't show them acting together). Clearing filters returns to the unfiltered list without re-mounting the screen (RF06 AC). |
72	| Export sheet | Meus Registros, download icon | 300ms debounce does not apply here (that's search only). Each stage change replaces the sheet content in place — the sheet itself never closes and reopens mid-job. |
73	| Offline banner / disabled send | Home/Chat | Disables sending only (`{colors.colorInfoOffline}` banner); history stays scrollable and readable. |
74	| Insertion modal, offline | "+" on Home/Chat while offline | Entry point is disabled with the same offline treatment as chat send — capture requires a live `POST /entries` round trip (PII check + embedding), so there is no local-only queued write. `[ASSUMPTION]`, grounded in RF06's AC ("offline allows only viewing cached data, not writing"). |
75	| Sign-up (Tela 0.1a, toggled) | "criar conta" link | Exactly two fields — email, senha — matching the prototype's login fields one-for-one. No name or password-confirmation field. `[ASSUMPTION]` (RNF08 visual fidelity; prototype shows no extra fields). |
76	
77	## State Patterns
78	
79	| State | Surface | Treatment |
80	|---|---|---|
81	| Biometric failure | Biometria | Falls through to PIN entry ("Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN") — never a dead end, never a lockout (RF03 AC). |
82	| Login/signup error | Entrar / Criar conta | `AUTH_INVALID` (wrong credentials, non-retryable) shows inline under the fields, same `{components.text-field.borderError}` treatment as any other validation error; `VALIDATION_ERROR` (malformed input, e.g. bad e-mail format) is caught before submit where possible. |
83	| New/empty chat | Home/Chat | Opened via "Novo Chat" with no messages yet — composer focused, no greeting copy invented beyond the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...". Distinct from a returning session, which restores the last conversation's scroll position. |
84	| Meus Registros — loading | Meus Registros | Skeleton rows (`DESIGN.md` skeleton component) only past the 300ms threshold (RNF01) while `GET /entries` resolves; under 300ms, no loading UI at all. |
85	| Session expired | Home/Chat (overlay) | Scrim over chat (still readable), card with lock icon, "Entrar novamente" → Biometria (not a full form). History and scroll position preserved in memory across re-auth. |
86	| Offline | Home/Chat | Send disabled, banner shown, history navigable. Same gating extends to the insertion-modal entry point (see Component Patterns). |
87	| Audio capture | Insertion modal, Áudio tab | Gravando → Processando (frozen/faded waveform) → Transcrito (editable) \| Erro ("Tentar novamente," audio never discarded). |
88	| Photo capture | Insertion modal, Foto tab | Captura → Processando OCR → Reconhecido (editable text) \| Erro (`OCR_NO_TEXT`, non-retryable — "Tentar novamente" re-invokes OCR on the same photo; secondary action "Salvar só a foto" saves the record with no extracted text). |
89	| Capture too large | Insertion modal, Áudio/Foto | `[ASSUMPTION]`: `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413, non-retryable) has no dedicated prototype state — reuse the red-warning visual language with a size-specific message, no retry button (retrying the same oversized file cannot succeed). |
90	| Export — preparing | Meus Registros → export sheet | `status=pending`. Spinner, no download. |
91	| Export — generating summary | export sheet | `status=processing`, `narrativeStatus=processing`. Progress bar, no download yet. |
92	| Export — data ready, summary still generating | export sheet | `[ASSUMPTION]` hybrid state the prototype's 5 visual states don't show (`docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`): `status=data_ready`, `narrativeStatus=processing`. Show "Baixar dados brutos" immediately (download available) while the summary-progress text keeps showing underneath — the raw data is never withheld waiting on the AI narrative. |
93	| Export — done, with summary | export sheet | `status=done`, `narrativeStatus=done`. "Resumo pronto," both download buttons. |
94	| Export — done, summary failed/skipped | export sheet | `status=done`, `narrativeStatus=failed\|skipped`. Error copy framed around the narrative only; "Baixar dados brutos" still enabled — raw data is never blocked by an AI failure (RF05 AC). |
95	| Export — error | export sheet | `status=error`. Includes `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` (period had zero entries) as one concrete cause — no download button, suggestion to adjust the filter. |
96	| Dashboard — zero entries | Configurações | Placeholder chart icon, "Comece a registrar..."; no summary paragraph (there is nothing to summarize — distinct from a narrative failure). |
97	| Dashboard — one entry | Configurações | Single bar, "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão..." |
98	| Dashboard — > 30 entries | Configurações | 10-bar chart + AI narrative paragraph. |
99	| Dashboard — narrative unavailable | Configurações | Chart renders normally with data; only the AI summary paragraph failed — needs its own distinct error message, never silently blank and never confused with the zero-entries empty state. |
100	| Sync badge | Record card | Synchronizing (local write pending server confirmation) / Error (write attempted and failed, retry available unless the underlying code is non-retryable) / Synchronized (confirmed) — all three inferred client-side from `updatedAt`/`serverRevision`, never sent ready-made by the server. |
101	| Chat response | Home/Chat | Streaming (pulsing cursor) → Complete, or → Failure (`"Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente"` in place of the timestamp; partial text stays visible, retried via the dedicated retry endpoint without duplicating the user's question). |
102	
103	## Interaction Primitives
104	
105	- Tap to act; the composer's send icon and every button follow the same primary-tap model — no double-tap, no force-touch.
106	- Text streaming reveals progressively with a blinking cursor; this is the one place motion carries meaning (the AI is actively responding) rather than decoration.
107	- Bottom sheets rise from the bottom (`sheetUp`, 0.2s); any overlay opening fades a scrim first (`scrimIn`, 0.18s). Both are the *only* entrance choreography in the system.
108	- PIN entry auto-advances 350ms after the 4th digit — no explicit "confirm" tap.
109	- **Banned:** swipe-to-delete or any swipe gesture on record cards (entries are immutable — there is no delete or edit endpoint on `/entries/:id`, so no gesture should imply one exists). Nested overlays (a sheet opening another sheet). Pull-to-refresh invented beyond what the spec defines (`GET /auth/session` and the chat/session streams already govern staleness — don't add a second, undefined refresh gesture on top). Long-press repurposed for anything other than native text selection.
110	
111	## Accessibility Floor
112	
113	Behavioral; visual contrast lives in `DESIGN.md`. `[ASSUMPTION]`: WCAG AA adopted as the floor even though `docs/input/requirements.md` does not mandate it — journaling content is personal, even though the product is explicitly not a mental-health app (no risk-signal protocol).
114	
115	- Every state that is currently color-only in the prototype (sync badge dot, bookmark states) must also carry an icon or an accessible label/announcement — color alone never carries state (see `DESIGN.md` Do's and Don'ts).
116	- Screen-reader labels announce transitions, not just static state: "Gravando," "Transcrevendo," "Erro ao transcrever, toque para tentar novamente."
117	- Dynamic type honored through `DESIGN.md` typography tokens; no control truncates at the largest accessibility text size (PIN keypad, filter chips and tab bar are the tightest-fit surfaces — verify first).
118	- Tap targets ≥ 44pt, including the bookmark icon and the sync-badge dot's tappable retry area (visually a small dot, hit area larger).
119	- Reduce Motion: skip the streaming cursor blink and `scrimIn`/`sheetUp` easing — show final state immediately; spinners become a static "carregando" label instead of a spin animation.
120	- Session-expired and account-deletion dialogs trap focus until dismissed or actioned — no interacting with the scrim-covered content underneath.
121	
122	## Inspiration & Anti-patterns
123	
124	- **Rejected — dynamic AI categorization:** simplified to manual, user-created tags (`docs/input/requirements.md` section 2). Don't reintroduce automatic tagging UI anywhere; tags are read-only, embedded, manual-only.
125	- **Rejected — autonomous goal extraction:** Planos de Ação is a static, non-functional kanban placeholder. Don't wire it to real data or real drag-and-drop — it exists only so the menu entry isn't broken.
126	- **Rejected — dynamic persona adjustment:** the three persona cards are a cosmetic toggle with no effect beyond (at most) a system-prompt string swap that isn't implemented. Don't let the UI imply the AI's behavior actually changes when a card is selected.
127	- **Rejected — clinical/therapeutic framing:** no mood tracking iconography, no "session" language borrowed from therapy apps, no crisis-support affordances — the product is explicit that it has no risk-signal detection and should not imply it does.
128	- **Rejected — gamification:** no streaks, no completion badges, no notification-driven re-engagement — none appear anywhere in the prototype or requirements, and introducing them would contradict the quiet, reflective posture in `DESIGN.md.Brand & Style`.
129	
130	## Key Flows
131	
132	### Flow 1 — Daily capture → reflection (Davi, after dinner, phone in hand)
133	
134	1. Davi opens the app; Face ID passes him straight to Home/Chat (last conversation still on screen).
135	   - *Auth failure branch (RF03):* if Face ID doesn't recognize him (gloves, bad angle), the barrier falls through to PIN entry with "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" — he's never locked out, just redirected to the alternate path.
136	2. He taps "+", lands on the Áudio tab, records 40 seconds about his day.
137	3. Recording stops; "Transcrevendo..." shows over the frozen waveform; transcript appears, editable. He fixes one word and taps "Salvar."
138	4. Modal closes; the new entry is on its way into the conversation's context, not into the chat thread itself.
139	5. He types a question to the AI referencing something from last week; the response streams in, grounded in his past entries (RAG).
140	6. **Climax:** mid-response, an insight card appears — "parece que você tem mencionado o trabalho com mais frequência essa semana" — surfacing a pattern Davi hadn't named himself. He doesn't dismiss it; he taps the bookmark on his own last message instead, saving the moment he connected the dot.
141	
142	Failure branch: if the transcription fails, the error state keeps the recorded audio and offers "Tentar novamente" — Davi never loses the 40 seconds he just spoke.
143	
144	### Flow 2 — Recall and export (Luiza, three months in, prepping for a check-in with her therapist)
145	
146	1. Luiza opens the side menu → Meus Registros.
147	2. She searches "ansiedade" in the search bar; results include an entry that only says "nervosismo" — semantic search surfaces it anyway.
148	3. She opens the filter sheet, narrows to "Este mês" + "áudio" — results re-narrow with AND logic; a "sincronizando" badge on her most recent card resolves to "sincronizado" moments later.
149	4. She taps the download icon → export sheet: "Preparando exportação..." → "Gerando resumo com IA..." with the raw-data download already available partway through.
150	5. **Climax:** "Resumo pronto." She downloads the PDF — a narrative summary of three months of entries, ready to bring into a conversation she'd been putting off.
151	
152	Failure branch: if the AI narrative fails, the sheet still offers "Baixar dados brutos" — her data was never hostage to the model call.
153	
154	### Flow 3 — Evolution check-in (Pedro, one month in, opens Settings out of curiosity)
155	
156	1. Pedro taps the side menu → Configurações.
157	2. The evolution dashboard computes on demand (RF09): with roughly a dozen entries so far, he sees the populated bar chart, not the one-entry or zero-entries placeholder.
158	3. He reads the AI-generated narrative paragraph below the chart — a plain-language read of his own pattern, not a diagnosis.
159	4. **Climax:** he notices the chart updated to include the entry he saved earlier that same day — the aggregation recalculated the moment he created it, not on some stale cache — proof the dashboard reflects *today's* Pedro, not last week's.
160	5. He taps the pencil beside his name to fix a typo; the field becomes editable in place, pencil turns to a check, and reverts to display mode on save.
161	
162	Failure branch: if the AI narrative fails independently of the chart, Pedro sees the populated chart with a distinct "narrative unavailable" message — never confused with having zero entries, and never a blank space where text should be.

status: final
updated: 2026-10-26
sources:
  - docs/input/requirements.md
  - docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md
  - docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html
  - docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md
  - docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md
  - docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md
---

# Cerne — Experience Spine

> Single-surface mobile (iOS, portrait only). Paired with `DESIGN.md`. The product spec and visual prototype are frozen and unusually complete — this spine resolves the handful of gaps the spec explicitly leaves open (marked `[ASSUMPTION]`) rather than inventing new UX surface. `Responsive & Platform` is omitted: there is exactly one form factor (390×844pt, portrait, iOS only).

## Foundation

Single-surface mobile, iOS only, portrait only, 390×844 logical points. No third-party UI system — fully custom per `DESIGN.md` tokens, implemented with Flutter + `flutter_bloc` + Clean Architecture (`docs/input/requirements.md` section 9/13). Language: Portuguese, single locale, no i18n layer. `DESIGN.md` is the visual-identity reference; this file is the experience — behavior, states, interaction, accessibility, flows. Light mode only; there is no dark-mode or theme-switching surface (see `DESIGN.md` Do's and Don'ts).

Three base screens hold almost everything; the rest are overlays on top of one of them, stacked at most one level deep:

- **Home/Chat** — default landing after auth.
- **Meus Registros** — consolidated timeline.
- **Configurações** — profile, dashboard, account.

## Information Architecture

| Surface | Reached from | Purpose | Backend-gated by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Splash (Tela 0) | Cold app launch | Checks session + syncs cache in background, auto-advances (1.8s) | `GET /auth/session` |
| Biometria / PIN (Tela 0.1) | Splash, "Sair," account deletion | Local access barrier before any user data is exposed | device-local; `POST /auth/login` only if the session fully expired |
| Entrar / Criar conta (Tela 0.1a) | "usar e-mail e senha" link on Biometria | Fallback credential auth, same screen toggled by mode | `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/signup` |
| Home/Chat (Tela 1) | Auth success, "Novo Chat," back from any overlay | Continuous conversation with the AI, entry point to capture | `POST/GET /chat/sessions`, `.../messages` |
| Insertion Modal (Tela 2) | "+" on Home/Chat | Multimodal capture — text / audio / photo — each produces a persisted entry, never a chat message | `POST /entries`, `POST /media/ocr` |
| Side menu (Tela 3) | ☰ on Home/Chat | Navigation hub: session history, My Records / Action Plans / Settings, new conversation | `GET /chat/sessions` |
| Meus Registros (Tela 4) | Side menu | Timeline, filter, search, export | `GET /entries`, `GET /entries/search`, `POST/GET /export/...` |
| Planos de Ação (Tela 5) `[ext]` | Side menu | Static 3-column kanban, placeholder only — no functional implementation | none (no backend calls) |
| Configurações (Tela 6) | Side menu | Profile editing, evolution dashboard, persona toggle `[ext]`, logout, account deletion | `GET /dashboard/...`, `PATCH /account/settings`, `DELETE /account`, `POST /auth/logout` |

No drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar — the side menu is the sole navigation hub besides the back arrow on Meus Registros and the "x" that closes any sheet/modal. Mirrors `docs/input/requirements.md` section 5.2 screen numbering and `prototype-extract.md` Tela numbering verbatim so both documents stay addressable by the same names.

→ **Composition reference:** `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html` — the frozen prototype is itself the 1:1, interactive visual reference for all 32 navigable states (`prototype-extract.md` sections 1-2); no separate static mock is generated, since it must never change. Open it directly and navigate by `screen` state/overlay flag to see any surface this table names. Spine wins on conflict.

## Voice and Tone

Microcopy only — brand posture and aesthetic register live in `DESIGN.md.Brand & Style`. Default voice leans **empático** — warm, validating, never clinical. `[ASSUMPTION]`: the prototype's three persona options (Analítico / Empático / Socrático) are a non-functional cosmetic toggle (`docs/input/requirements.md` section 2), so the product must ship with exactly one real voice regardless of which card looks selected.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| "Não foi possível transcrever" / "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto" — exact prototype copy, factual, no blame | "Oops! Something went wrong 😢" |
| "Sessão expirada" with a plain explanation that history is kept | Any language implying data loss or starting over |
| Insight copy that surfaces a pattern ("parece que..., você mencionou...") without diagnosing or prescribing | Therapeutic framing, diagnostic language, or crisis-support claims — the product explicitly has no risk-signal protocol (`docs/input/requirements.md` section 4, known limitation) |
| "Resumo pronto" / "Baixar dados brutos" — plain, factual labels | Celebratory language around export or streaks around journaling frequency |
| Second person, direct ("Toque para desbloquear") | Infantilizing or over-familiar tone |

## Component Patterns

Behavioral; visual specs live in `DESIGN.md.Components`.

| Component | Use | Behavioral rules |
|---|---|---|
| Insertion modal tab bar | Texto / Áudio / Foto | Opening the modal always resets all three tabs to idle/empty. Switching tabs while a capture is actively in flight (recording, or OCR/transcription processing) **cancels that capture outright** — no partial entry is created, applying RF01's existing cancel-on-interrupt rule to this trigger. `[ASSUMPTION]` (prototype leaves this undefined). |
| Chat bubble / message | Home/Chat | User bubbles are static once sent. AI bubbles alone carry a state machine: streaming (`{colors.colorTextPrimary}` text revealed progressively behind a blinking cursor) → complete, or → failure (timestamp slot replaced by red retry copy, bubble content never cleared). |
| Bookmark button (RF10) | Every user chat message | idle → saving → saved/error. Tapping an already-`saved` message is a no-op (idempotent per RF10 AC — same message never creates a duplicate entry). `error` returns to a retryable idle-like state, never stuck. Only user messages carry the button — AI responses never do. |
| Insight card (RF08) | Interleaved in chat | Fires once per satisfied trigger (5 user messages OR 2 min inactivity) — never both, never twice for the same window. Dismiss ("x") never changes scroll position or chat state. Failure to generate is silent to the user — chat continues uninterrupted. |
| Sync badge | Record card (Meus Registros) | Tap on an `error` badge (`{colors.colorError}` dot) retries that entry's write. `[ASSUMPTION]`, grounded in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`: the error means a local write was attempted and failed, so content is still held client-side and retry is meaningful. If the underlying error code is non-retryable (see State Patterns), show an inline explanation instead of a retry affordance. |
| Avatar — inline name editing | Configurações | Tapping the pencil beside the name/e-mail switches that field to an editable text input in place; the pencil icon becomes a check. Confirming commits via `PATCH /account/settings`; the field reverts to display mode either on save or on tapping elsewhere. No separate "edit profile" screen. |
| Record card | Meus Registros | Display-only — tapping a card does nothing beyond revealing its sync badge's retry affordance when in `error` state. No detail screen exists; entries are immutable, so no tap-to-edit or tap-to-expand behavior should be implied. |
| Search bar + filter sheet | Meus Registros | Query text and active filter chips combine with **AND** logic against the same `GET /entries/search` call — consistent with RF06's multi-filter AND rule. `[ASSUMPTION]` (prototype doesn't show them acting together). Clearing filters returns to the unfiltered list without re-mounting the screen (RF06 AC). |
| Export sheet | Meus Registros, download icon | 300ms debounce does not apply here (that's search only). Each stage change replaces the sheet content in place — the sheet itself never closes and reopens mid-job. |
| Offline banner / disabled send | Home/Chat | Disables sending only (`{colors.colorInfoOffline}` banner); history stays scrollable and readable. |
| Insertion modal, offline | "+" on Home/Chat while offline | Entry point is disabled with the same offline treatment as chat send — capture requires a live `POST /entries` round trip (PII check + embedding), so there is no local-only queued write. `[ASSUMPTION]`, grounded in RF06's AC ("offline allows only viewing cached data, not writing"). |
| Sign-up (Tela 0.1a, toggled) | "criar conta" link | Exactly two fields — email, senha — matching the prototype's login fields one-for-one. No name or password-confirmation field. `[ASSUMPTION]` (RNF08 visual fidelity; prototype shows no extra fields). |

## State Patterns

| State | Surface | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Biometric failure | Biometria | Falls through to PIN entry ("Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN") — never a dead end, never a lockout (RF03 AC). |
| Login/signup error | Entrar / Criar conta | `AUTH_INVALID` (wrong credentials, non-retryable) shows inline under the fields, same `{components.text-field.borderError}` treatment as any other validation error; `VALIDATION_ERROR` (malformed input, e.g. bad e-mail format) is caught before submit where possible. |
| New/empty chat | Home/Chat | Opened via "Novo Chat" with no messages yet — composer focused, no greeting copy invented beyond the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...". Distinct from a returning session, which restores the last conversation's scroll position. |
| Meus Registros — loading | Meus Registros | Skeleton rows (`DESIGN.md` skeleton component) only past the 300ms threshold (RNF01) while `GET /entries` resolves; under 300ms, no loading UI at all. |
| Session expired | Home/Chat (overlay) | Scrim over chat (still readable), card with lock icon, "Entrar novamente" → Biometria (not a full form). History and scroll position preserved in memory across re-auth. |
| Offline | Home/Chat | Send disabled, banner shown, history navigable. Same gating extends to the insertion-modal entry point (see Component Patterns). |
| Audio capture | Insertion modal, Áudio tab | Gravando → Processando (frozen/faded waveform) → Transcrito (editable) \| Erro ("Tentar novamente," audio never discarded). |
| Photo capture | Insertion modal, Foto tab | Captura → Processando OCR → Reconhecido (editable text) \| Erro (`OCR_NO_TEXT`, non-retryable — "Tentar novamente" re-invokes OCR on the same photo; secondary action "Salvar só a foto" saves the record with no extracted text). |
| Capture too large | Insertion modal, Áudio/Foto | `[ASSUMPTION]`: `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413, non-retryable) has no dedicated prototype state — reuse the red-warning visual language with a size-specific message, no retry button (retrying the same oversized file cannot succeed). |
| Export — preparing | Meus Registros → export sheet | `status=pending`. Spinner, no download. |
| Export — generating summary | export sheet | `status=processing`, `narrativeStatus=processing`. Progress bar, no download yet. |
| Export — data ready, summary still generating | export sheet | `[ASSUMPTION]` hybrid state the prototype's 5 visual states don't show (`docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`): `status=data_ready`, `narrativeStatus=processing`. Show "Baixar dados brutos" immediately (download available) while the summary-progress text keeps showing underneath — the raw data is never withheld waiting on the AI narrative. |
| Export — done, with summary | export sheet | `status=done`, `narrativeStatus=done`. "Resumo pronto," both download buttons. |
| Export — done, summary failed/skipped | export sheet | `status=done`, `narrativeStatus=failed\|skipped`. Error copy framed around the narrative only; "Baixar dados brutos" still enabled — raw data is never blocked by an AI failure (RF05 AC). |
| Export — error | export sheet | `status=error`. Includes `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` (period had zero entries) as one concrete cause — no download button, suggestion to adjust the filter. |
| Dashboard — zero entries | Configurações | Placeholder chart icon, "Comece a registrar..."; no summary paragraph (there is nothing to summarize — distinct from a narrative failure). |
| Dashboard — one entry | Configurações | Single bar, "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão..." |
| Dashboard — > 30 entries | Configurações | 10-bar chart + AI narrative paragraph. |
| Dashboard — narrative unavailable | Configurações | Chart renders normally with data; only the AI summary paragraph failed — needs its own distinct error message, never silently blank and never confused with the zero-entries empty state. |
| Sync badge | Record card | Synchronizing (local write pending server confirmation) / Error (write attempted and failed, retry available unless the underlying code is non-retryable) / Synchronized (confirmed) — all three inferred client-side from `updatedAt`/`serverRevision`, never sent ready-made by the server. |
| Chat response | Home/Chat | Streaming (pulsing cursor) → Complete, or → Failure (`"Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente"` in place of the timestamp; partial text stays visible, retried via the dedicated retry endpoint without duplicating the user's question). |

## Interaction Primitives

- Tap to act; the composer's send icon and every button follow the same primary-tap model — no double-tap, no force-touch.
- Text streaming reveals progressively with a blinking cursor; this is the one place motion carries meaning (the AI is actively responding) rather than decoration.
- Bottom sheets rise from the bottom (`sheetUp`, 0.2s); any overlay opening fades a scrim first (`scrimIn`, 0.18s). Both are the *only* entrance choreography in the system.
- PIN entry auto-advances 350ms after the 4th digit — no explicit "confirm" tap.
- **Banned:** swipe-to-delete or any swipe gesture on record cards (entries are immutable — there is no delete or edit endpoint on `/entries/:id`, so no gesture should imply one exists). Nested overlays (a sheet opening another sheet). Pull-to-refresh invented beyond what the spec defines (`GET /auth/session` and the chat/session streams already govern staleness — don't add a second, undefined refresh gesture on top). Long-press repurposed for anything other than native text selection.

## Accessibility Floor

Behavioral; visual contrast lives in `DESIGN.md`. `[ASSUMPTION]`: WCAG AA adopted as the floor even though `docs/input/requirements.md` does not mandate it — journaling content is personal, even though the product is explicitly not a mental-health app (no risk-signal protocol).

- Every state that is currently color-only in the prototype (sync badge dot, bookmark states) must also carry an icon or an accessible label/announcement — color alone never carries state (see `DESIGN.md` Do's and Don'ts).
- Screen-reader labels announce transitions, not just static state: "Gravando," "Transcrevendo," "Erro ao transcrever, toque para tentar novamente."
- Dynamic type honored through `DESIGN.md` typography tokens; no control truncates at the largest accessibility text size (PIN keypad, filter chips and tab bar are the tightest-fit surfaces — verify first).
- Tap targets ≥ 44pt, including the bookmark icon and the sync-badge dot's tappable retry area (visually a small dot, hit area larger).
- Reduce Motion: skip the streaming cursor blink and `scrimIn`/`sheetUp` easing — show final state immediately; spinners become a static "carregando" label instead of a spin animation.
- Session-expired and account-deletion dialogs trap focus until dismissed or actioned — no interacting with the scrim-covered content underneath.

## Inspiration & Anti-patterns

- **Rejected — dynamic AI categorization:** simplified to manual, user-created tags (`docs/input/requirements.md` section 2). Don't reintroduce automatic tagging UI anywhere; tags are read-only, embedded, manual-only.
- **Rejected — autonomous goal extraction:** Planos de Ação is a static, non-functional kanban placeholder. Don't wire it to real data or real drag-and-drop — it exists only so the menu entry isn't broken.
- **Rejected — dynamic persona adjustment:** the three persona cards are a cosmetic toggle with no effect beyond (at most) a system-prompt string swap that isn't implemented. Don't let the UI imply the AI's behavior actually changes when a card is selected.
- **Rejected — clinical/therapeutic framing:** no mood tracking iconography, no "session" language borrowed from therapy apps, no crisis-support affordances — the product is explicit that it has no risk-signal detection and should not imply it does.
- **Rejected — gamification:** no streaks, no completion badges, no notification-driven re-engagement — none appear anywhere in the prototype or requirements, and introducing them would contradict the quiet, reflective posture in `DESIGN.md.Brand & Style`.

## Key Flows

### Flow 1 — Daily capture → reflection (Davi, after dinner, phone in hand)

1. Davi opens the app; Face ID passes him straight to Home/Chat (last conversation still on screen).
   - *Auth failure branch (RF03):* if Face ID doesn't recognize him (gloves, bad angle), the barrier falls through to PIN entry with "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" — he's never locked out, just redirected to the alternate path.

6. **Climax:** mid-response, an insight card appears — "parece que você tem mencionado o trabalho com mais frequência essa semana" — surfacing a pattern Davi hadn't named himself. He doesn't dismiss it; he taps the bookmark on his own last message instead, saving the moment he connected the dot.

Failure branch: if the transcription fails, the error state keeps the recorded audio and offers "Tentar novamente" — Davi never loses the 40 seconds he just spoke.

### Flow 2 — Recall and export (Luiza, three months in, prepping for a check-in with her therapist)

1. Luiza opens the side menu → Meus Registros.
2. She searches "ansiedade" in the search bar; results include an entry that only says "nervosismo" — semantic search surfaces it anyway.
3. She opens the filter sheet, narrows to "Este mês" + "áudio" — results re-narrow with AND logic; a "sincronizando" badge on her most recent card resolves to "sincronizado" moments later.
4. She taps the download icon → export sheet: "Preparando exportação..." → "Gerando resumo com IA..." with the raw-data download already available partway through.
5. **Climax:** "Resumo pronto." She downloads the PDF — a narrative summary of three months of entries, ready to bring into a conversation she'd been putting off.

### Flow 3 — Evolution check-in (Pedro, one month in, opens Settings out of curiosity)

1. Pedro taps the side menu → Configurações.
2. The evolution dashboard computes on demand (RF09): with roughly a dozen entries so far, he sees the populated bar chart, not the one-entry or zero-entries placeholder.
3. He reads the AI-generated narrative paragraph below the chart — a plain-language read of his own pattern, not a diagnosis.
4. **Climax:** he notices the chart updated to include the entry he saved earlier that same day — the aggregation recalculated the moment he created it, not on some stale cache — proof the dashboard reflects *today's* Pedro, not last week's.

# Cerne - Epic Breakdown

## Overview

This document provides the complete epic and story breakdown for Cerne, decomposing the requirements from the PRD, UX Design contract, and Architecture Spine into implementable stories.

## Requirements Inventory

### Functional Requirements

**4.1 Foundation & Session Management (F000)**

- FR-1: Account creation and authentication — signup, login, silent refresh/session-check, all round-tripping through the backend and surfacing the Failure contract on error; a valid session persists across app restarts without re-prompting. `[ASSUMPTION]` signup collects email + password only (PRD OQ-2).
- FR-2: Expired-session recovery overlay — a "Sessão expirada" overlay appears over the current screen (never navigates away) when the backend reports an expired session; "Entrar novamente" routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow (RF03), not a login form; screen state/scroll position preserved underneath.
- FR-3: Base navigation shell — navigation between Home/Chat, side menu, Meus Registros, and Configurações reachable from launch, with visually distinguishable placeholders for not-yet-built RF01–RF10 functionality.

**4.2 Biometric Authentication Vault (RF03)**

- FR-4: App-access gate — Face ID/Touch ID/PIN required before any user data is shown, on cold start and after the idle timeout (FR-6); no biometric data or call ever reaches the backend.
- FR-5: Biometric-failure fallback to PIN — a failed biometric attempt always offers a reachable PIN path; never locks the user out; an OS-level lockout is detected and routed to the app's own PIN fallback.
- FR-6: Fixed idle re-authentication timeout — 5 minutes backgrounded triggers re-auth on resume; fixed, not user-configurable.
- FR-7: Biometric preference persistence — enable/disable biometric gating is saved via `PATCH /account/settings`, survives restarts and reinstalls (fetched from account, not cached locally only); disabling biometrics still leaves PIN as the access method.

**4.3 Multimodal Capture (RF01)**

- FR-8: Text Entry capture — free text typed in the Insertion Modal saved as an Entry (`source=manual`).
- FR-9: Audio Entry capture — audio recorded in the Insertion Modal becomes the basis of an Entry (`source=audio`) once processed (RF02).
- FR-10: Photo Entry capture — a captured/selected photo becomes the basis of an Entry (`source=photo`) once processed (RF02). *(FR-8–10 consequence: all three modalities produce the same persisted Entry shape; each `POST /entries` call carries the correct `source`.)*
- FR-11: Cancel-safe capture — interrupting a capture in progress (stop before saving, back out mid-photo) never creates a partial/empty Entry; no `POST /entries` call fires for an abandoned capture. `[OPEN]` tab-switch mid-capture behavior (PRD OQ-3) — resolved by UX-DR25 below: cancels the in-flight capture outright.

**4.4 Speech-to-Text / OCR Processing (RF02)**

- FR-12: On-device audio transcription — audio is transcribed to text entirely on-device via `whisper_ggml`; the audio file itself is never sent to the backend. Four states in sequence: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry, media never discarded.
- FR-13: Backend OCR for photos — a captured photo is sent to `POST /media/ocr` to extract text before the Entry is created. Mirrors FR-12's four-state pattern; on failure, two recovery paths exist (retry OCR, or "Salvar só a foto" with no extracted text); `OCR_NO_TEXT` is a distinct, user-visible, non-retryable outcome.

**4.5 Multi-Source History / Timeline (RF07)**

- FR-14: Chronological Entry list — all Entries from any source listed together, grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.
- FR-15: Per-entry Sync Badge — one of three states (Synchronizing / Synchronization error / Synchronized), derived client-side from `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` plus local pending-write state; the badge stream is independent of the auth/session stream. `[OPEN]` no retry affordance visible in the prototype (PRD OQ-6) — resolved by UX-DR30 below.
- FR-16: Empty-state handling — zero Entries shows a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture, not a blank list.
- FR-17: Session-expiry resilience mid-view — the FR-2 overlay appears over the timeline without crashing or losing scroll position.
- FR-18: Entry detail view — a single Entry can be opened from the timeline via `GET /entries/:id`; never mutates it (no edit affordance); a detail request for another user's/nonexistent Entry returns `NOT_FOUND` (RNF04). *Feature-specific NFR: no BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly — the auth-status, Sync-Badge-state, and Entry-data streams combine only through the domain layer.*

**4.6 Semantic Search / Filter (RF06)**

- FR-19: Semantic search — meaning-based search over Entries (not literal keyword match) via `GET /entries/search`.
- FR-20: Metadata filters — filter by source and date range (`dateFrom`/`dateTo`), no tag/category filter; no-search-term filtering queries `GET /entries`, filtering + active search term queries `GET /entries/search` with the same filter params. *(FR-19/20 consequence: multiple active filters combine with AND semantics.)* `[OPEN]` search+filter interaction (PRD OQ-7) — resolved by UX-DR29 below: AND-combine against `GET /entries/search`.
- FR-21: Debounced search input — 300ms debounce before firing a request.
- FR-22: Non-disruptive filter clearing — clearing filters restores the full list in place (no full reload); cache stays duplicate-free after a reconnect (cloud-only; offline is view-only here).

**4.7 Interactive Chat with Memory / RAG (RF04)**

- FR-23: Send message, receive RAG-grounded streaming response — via SSE on `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`; exactly three visible states (streaming/processing, error, complete); Chat Messages never automatically create Entries (RF10 is the sole exception).
- FR-24: Multi-session chat history — multiple named Chat Sessions, listed and switchable from the side menu.
- FR-25: New-conversation action — start a new Chat Session from the side menu; `POST /chat/sessions` is blocked offline.
- FR-26: Dropped-stream resilience — if a response stream drops mid-generation, the partial message stays on screen with a failure indicator; retryable via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` without duplicating the original question.
- FR-27: Offline composer lock — composer disabled while offline; existing conversation history stays visible and navigable.

**4.8 Save Chat Message as Entry (RF10)** — depends on RF01, RF04

- FR-28: Bookmark a user message into an Entry — a "save" affordance on the user's own Chat Messages only (never AI responses) creates an Entry (`source=chat`, carrying `chatMessageId`) through the same shared entries use case RF01 defines, never by importing the entries repository/data source directly (RNF06).
- FR-29: Idempotent save — saving the same Chat Message more than once never creates a duplicate Entry and never surfaces a conflict error (backend returns 200, not 409).
- FR-30: Save-failure isolation — on save failure, the surrounding Chat Session stays fully usable; the save affordance resets to a retryable state rather than freezing.

**4.9 Proactive Insights (RF08)** — depends on RF04; scope is trigger/injection mechanism only, generated-text quality out of scope

- FR-31: Unprompted Insight injection — injected into the active Chat Session once per satisfied condition (5 user messages OR 2 minutes inactivity, whichever first) via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight`.
- FR-32: Insight failure isolation — a failed Insight generation never interrupts or breaks the main chat experience; composer stays enabled, no error overlay, ordinary chat messages keep working.
- FR-33: Non-disruptive dismissal — dismissing an Insight never affects scroll position or other conversation state.

**4.10 Personal Summary Export (RF05)** — depends on RF07; scope is job/file/failure handling only, generated-narrative quality out of scope

- FR-34: Request a period export — via `POST /export/summary` for a chosen date period.
- FR-35: Job status across five screen states — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio — via `GET /export/:jobId/status`, reporting `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) independently.
- FR-36: Narrative-independent raw-data download — raw data downloadable via `GET /export/:jobId/download` as soon as ready, even if the narrative step is still processing, failed, or skipped; the narrative never blocks the download.
- FR-37: Empty-period handling — an export request for a period with zero Entries surfaces "Período vazio," no download offered, no crash.

**4.11 Temporal Summaries / Dashboard & Account (RF09)** — depends on F000, RF01; Dashboard scope is aggregation/rendering only, narrative-text quality out of scope

- FR-38: On-demand dashboard aggregation — opening Configurações computes/renders an evolution chart via `GET /dashboard/aggregate`, correctly at zero, one, and >30 Entries.
- FR-39: Independent narrative text — fetched via `GET /dashboard/narrative`; its failure is a distinct, chart-still-renders state, never blocking the chart (two independent endpoints by design).
- FR-40: Cache invalidation on new Entry — dashboard aggregation recalculates after a new Entry is created elsewhere in the app; invalidation only ever triggers on create (Entries are immutable, never edited).
- FR-41: Profile name editing — inline display-name edit on Configurações via `PATCH /account/settings`.
- FR-42: Logout — "Sair" ends the session (`POST /auth/logout`) and returns to the Biometric Vault / login screen.
- FR-43: Account deletion — "Apagar conta" shows a confirmation dialog; on confirm, account and all data are hard-deleted (`DELETE /account`, LGPD-driven); routes to the same destination as logout. `[NOTE]` no dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists (PRD OQ-4).

### NonFunctional Requirements

- RNF01 (performance): local UI interactions respond in <100ms; any network call taking >300ms shows a loading indicator. Verified by manual timing spot-check per feature module (no automated perf instrumentation planned).
- RNF02 (PII handling) `[inherited, not verified by this delivery]`: PII stripping runs server-side via a Claude Haiku 4.5 structured prompt/tool-use step.
- RNF03 (data retention) `[inherited, not verified by this delivery]`: zero data retention by upstream AI providers.
- RNF04 (data isolation): Row Level Security (Supabase) enforces per-user data isolation; client never needs its own cross-user authorization logic; the backend uniformly returns `NOT_FOUND` (never permission-denied) for another user's resource.
- RNF05 (account deletion): hard delete of account and all associated data on request (LGPD).
- RNF06 (architecture): zero Clean Architecture layer violations — the domain layer imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything from a `data/` layer, across all 11 feature modules.
- RNF07 (test coverage): ≥80% domain-layer test coverage.
- RNF08 (visual fidelity): visual fidelity to the prototype (color, typography, spacing); zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`.
- RNF09 (resilience): every repository returns `Either<Failure, T>`; 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types (timeout, malformed response, no connection) = 15 tested failure scenarios, zero unhandled exceptions.

### Additional Requirements

*(from the Architecture Spine — cross-unit invariants and stack decisions that bound how stories must be implemented; binds column shows which build units each rule applies to)*

- Delivery order governs epic/story sequencing: F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09 — later units assume earlier ones exist (e.g., RF10 assumes RF01 and RF04 are both done). No reordering.
- **Integration spike required first, inside F000, before any other building:** verify `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` work together in one scaffold bootstrap — flagged as unverified in combination even though each package is independently current.
- AD-1 (binds: all) — strict layer dependency direction `presentation → domain ← data`; only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins; `presentation/` never imports any `data/` directly.
- AD-2 (binds: all repositories) — every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream); no native/dio exception escapes unmapped.
- AD-3 (binds: all) — one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes (13 from `error-taxonomy.md` + local-only `MalformedResponse`); never redefined or subset per feature; `AuthInvalid` only ever originates from `POST /auth/login`.
- AD-4 (binds: the API client) — retry logic implemented exactly once (the `dio` interceptor/`ApiClient` wrapper), fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes; every other code surfaces once, unretried.
- AD-5 (binds: every network call) — one URL builder in `core/` maps each operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>`; one `dio` interceptor owns headers (`apikey` always; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` only on signup/login/refresh; `Authorization: Bearer <user token>` otherwise).
- AD-6 (binds: RF01 introduces `features/entries/`; RF10 and any future cross-feature dependency consume it) — `entries/domain` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port, and the Hive box; RF01's `capture` and RF10's `chat` are consumers only (import the abstract port, never `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`); RF06/RF07 extend the same port with `list`/`search`, never a second entry model; `create` is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`.
- AD-7 (binds: all) — a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency; composition via injected domain streams/use-cases or `BlocListener`/`MultiBlocListener`.
- AD-8 (binds: F000, RF07, any session-consuming feature) — exactly one `SessionStatus` stream from the auth feature's `domain/`, registered once in DI as a singleton; no consumer re-derives session state from a raw 401 or a second stream.
- AD-9 (binds: all repositories) — a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)`, never queued; plain reads fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache; semantic search (`GET /entries/search`) has no client-side vector index, so it also resolves to `networkOffline` when offline, same as a write.
- AD-10 (binds: every screen rendering the sync badge) — one derivation function in `entries/domain`, computed from `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and transient per-entry write state; every screen consumes that function's output, none recomputes inline.
- AD-11 (binds: the entries feature) — `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read only; no update/delete method is ever added.
- AD-12 (binds: RF06, RF09 — explicitly not RF02/RF04/RF07) — generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) in `core/` used only by single-data-source, single-fetch-lifecycle screens; RF02, RF04, and RF07 each define their own sealed state class.
- AD-13 (binds: RF08, RF10) — `core/` holds a never-throws `isolatedSideEffect` helper (`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped), ships with RF10 (first consumer); RF10 may `await` it, RF08 must call it fire-and-forget (without awaiting).
- AD-14 (binds: F000 builds the redirect skeleton + `SessionStatus` half; RF03 plugs in the vault half) — one `go_router` redirect composing exactly two gates in fixed order: `VaultStatus` first, then `SessionStatus`; neither gate ever reaches the server to validate itself.
- AD-15 (binds: `entries`, `chat` — every feature with a `hive_ce` box) — every query dimension (source, date range, semantic search, pagination cursor) is a server-side query parameter; a Hive box stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id; no feature filters/joins/sorts/re-derives a cached collection locally.
- Stack pins (binding on F000, verified at scaffold time): Flutter SDK 3.47.x stable family (exact patch pinned via `fvm`), `flutter_bloc` ^9.1.1, `go_router` ^18.1.1, `dio` ^5.11.1, `hive_ce`/`hive_ce_flutter` ^2.22.0, `get_it` ^9.3.0, `fpdart` ^1.2.0, `freezed`/`freezed_annotation` ^4.0.3, `json_serializable` ^6.15.2, `build_runner` (latest compatible), `mocktail` ^1.0.5, `fl_chart` ^1.3.0, `local_auth` ^3.0.2, `flutter_secure_storage` ^11.2.0, `flutter_dotenv` ^6.0.1, `whisper_ggml` ^2.8.1.
- Structural seed (binding on F000, extended by each feature's own build unit): `lib/core/` (`design_tokens.dart`, `network/`, `failure/`, `di/`, `cache/`, `resource.dart`, `isolated_side_effect.dart`, `session/`) and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each three-layered (`data/domain/presentation`).
- Config/secrets: `.env` (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) loaded via `flutter_dotenv`; never committed, never hardcoded.
- Testing convention (binding at every feature's test suite): `mocktail` stubs one `ApiClient` interface per repository test; one shared table-driven helper drives the 15-scenario (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types) matrix; ≥80% line coverage gate on every `domain/`.
- No starter/greenfield template is specified — the app is scaffolded directly per the Structural Seed above, not from a community starter kit.

### UX Design Requirements

*(from `DESIGN.md` + `EXPERIENCE.md` — actionable design-token, component, accessibility, and interaction work; each item is specific enough to generate its own story-level acceptance criteria)*

**Design tokens**

- UX-DR1: Implement the full token set (`colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`) from `DESIGN.md`'s frontmatter verbatim into `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` as the single source of truth (RNF08) — camelCase names map 1:1, zero translation step. Includes the two elevation values (`elevation1`, `elevation2`) inlined as literal shadow strings since they aren't in the frontmatter token categories.

**Reusable components (list all, not summarized)**

- UX-DR2: Button components — primary (filled, darkens on press), secondary (outline), text/ghost (no chrome); disabled state always `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text, never a dimmed opacity of the active state.
- UX-DR3: Text field component with default/focused (`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error (`colorError`) border states.
- UX-DR4: Chat bubble components — user (sage, square bottom-right, static once sent) vs. AI (ivory, `elevation1`, square bottom-left, streaming state adds a blinking cursor at text end, no other visual change while generating).
- UX-DR5: Insight card component — ochre spine on the left edge (the only accent-colored element inside the chat stream), mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x."
- UX-DR6: Bookmark button component — four states (idle/saving/saved/error) on every user message only, never on AI responses; state carried by icon + color together, never color alone; tapping an already-`saved` message is a no-op; `error` returns to a retryable idle-like state.
- UX-DR7: Sync badge component — small dot (green/ochre/red for synced/synchronizing/error), reinforced by an accessible label on tap/long-focus since dot color alone is insufficient; tap on `error` retries that entry's write when the underlying code is retryable, shows inline explanation instead when non-retryable (resolves PRD OQ-6).
- UX-DR8: Filter chip component — sage background, dark-olive text, fully rounded; single-choice (date range) and multi-choice (category/type) look visually identical, differ only in behavior.
- UX-DR9: Search bar component — paper-elevated input, trailing funnel icon button, permanently docked at top of Meus Registros, never submitted with a button, 300ms debounce.
- UX-DR10: Filter sheet component — `radiusLg`/`elevation2` bottom sheet, groups labeled in `textMonoCaption`.
- UX-DR11: Insertion-modal tab bar component — three equal-width segments (Texto/Áudio/Foto); active segment alone gets filled `colorPrimary` background.
- UX-DR12: Audio waveform component — animated bars in the structural palette while recording; frozen at 35% opacity while processing (no additional label needed beyond the "Transcrevendo..." text).
- UX-DR13: Avatar component — solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials in `colorOnPrimary`, two fixed sizes (40px menu, 52px Settings), no photo avatars anywhere; in Configurações the pencil icon becomes a check icon in edit mode.
- UX-DR14: PIN keypad component — numeric 3×4 grid + backspace, progress dots above, structural palette only (no accent on digits), auto-advances 350ms after the 4th digit with no explicit confirm tap.
- UX-DR15: Export sheet component — heaviest surface after a full-screen modal (`radiusLg`+`elevation2`); each job-stage change replaces sheet content in place, the sheet itself never closes/reopens mid-job.
- UX-DR16: Confirmation dialog component — neutral title (`colorTextPrimary`) for session expiry, red title (`colorError`) for destructive deletion; title color is the only signal distinguishing the two, so it must never be muted; traps focus until dismissed/actioned.
- UX-DR17: Skeleton loading component — shown only past the 300ms threshold (RNF01), `colorBorder`-toned shimmer (never a spinner), for content loading only.
- UX-DR18: Record card component — spine colored by Entry origin (manual=`colorPrimary`, audio=olive green, photo=gray, chat=`colorAccent`); the only place color encodes a data dimension rather than a UI state.
- UX-DR19: Banner components — offline banner (`colorInfoOffline`, single-use, offline only) and send-error banner (muted red wash); never reuse the offline blue-gray for any other informational banner.

**Accessibility**

- UX-DR20: WCAG AA adopted as the accessibility floor (not mandated by requirements.md, adopted here); every currently color-only state (sync badge dot, bookmark states) also carries an icon or accessible label — color alone never carries state.
- UX-DR21: Screen-reader labels announce transitions, not just static state ("Gravando," "Transcrevendo," "Erro ao transcrever, toque para tentar novamente").
- UX-DR22: Dynamic type honored at every level; no control truncates/clips at the largest accessibility text size — PIN keypad, filter chips, and tab bar are the tightest-fit surfaces and must be verified first.
- UX-DR23: Tap targets ≥44pt, including the bookmark icon and the sync-badge dot's retry hit area (visually a small dot, hit area larger).
- UX-DR24: Reduce Motion support — skip the streaming cursor blink and `scrimIn`/`sheetUp` easing (show final state immediately); spinners become a static "carregando" label instead of a spin animation.
- UX-DR25: Session-expired and account-deletion dialogs trap focus until dismissed or actioned — no interacting with scrim-covered content underneath.

**Interaction patterns**

- UX-DR26: Insertion-modal tab-switch mid-capture cancels the in-flight capture outright (recording or OCR/transcription processing) — no partial entry created; opening the modal always resets all three tabs to idle/empty. Resolves PRD OQ-3.
- UX-DR27: Entrance choreography limited to exactly two animations system-wide: `sheetUp` (0.2s, bottom sheets) and `scrimIn` (0.18s, any overlay's scrim) — no other motion.
- UX-DR28: Banned gestures enforced everywhere: no swipe-to-delete (or any swipe) on record cards, no nested overlays (a sheet opening another sheet), no pull-to-refresh beyond the spec-defined refresh points, no long-press repurposed beyond native text selection.
- UX-DR29: Search bar query text + active filter chips combine with AND logic against the same `GET /entries/search` call; clearing filters returns to the unfiltered list without re-mounting the screen. Resolves PRD OQ-7.
- UX-DR30: Offline disables the insertion-modal "+" entry point with the same offline treatment as chat send (capture requires a live `POST /entries` round trip for PII check + embedding — no local-only queued write).
- UX-DR31: Signup screen has exactly two fields (email, senha), matching the prototype's login fields one-for-one — no name or password-confirmation field. Resolves PRD OQ-2.

**Visual/state standardization**

- UX-DR32: Extension/placeholder screens (Planos de Ação kanban, persona toggle cards) are styled with full visual polish — never marked as visibly "unfinished" or grayed-out, despite having no functional logic behind them.
- UX-DR33: Dashboard renders four distinct states: zero entries (placeholder icon + "Comece a registrar..."), one entry (single bar + "Ainda é cedo..."), >30 entries (10-bar chart + narrative), and narrative-unavailable (chart renders normally, only the AI summary paragraph shows a distinct failure message — never blank, never confused with zero-entries).
- UX-DR34: Export sheet renders the hybrid "data ready, summary still generating" state (`status=data_ready`, `narrativeStatus=processing`) not present in the prototype's original 5 visual states — "Baixar dados brutos" shown immediately while summary-progress text keeps showing underneath.
- UX-DR35: Single fixed frame 390×844 logical points, portrait only, single column, light mode only — no tablet/landscape/dark-mode layout to reconcile against.
- UX-DR36: Overlays stack at most one level deep — a bottom sheet or dialog sits on a darkened scrim over exactly one base screen; the insertion modal's three tabs are internal states of one sheet, not nested sheets.
